items.title: India's cartoonists built an audience online - now their posts are being restricted
items.summary: Indian cartoonists say online restrictions are making satire harder, but they aren't giving up.
items.content:
For the second time in three weeks, Indian cartoonist Satish Acharya found himself effectively invisible on Instagram in his own country.

The 55-year-old discovered on Tuesday that his account had once again been briefly blocked in India, allegedly with no explanation from the platform.

Just a few weeks ago, another cartoonist, Manjul, had found that Instagram had restricted a post criticising India's election commission over its controversial revision of voter rolls. His profile remained accessible.

The cases have raised concerns about the use of legal orders to restrict political satire in India, with cartoonists saying they are often given little explanation for why their work has been blocked.

Acharaya's account was first restricted from 28 September to 6 October, when users in India could neither find his profile through search nor access it through a web link.

Anyone trying to access his profile saw a message saying it was unavailable under India's Information Technology Rules.

The rules allow authorities and courts to order social media platforms to remove or restrict content.

The government says they help tackle unlawful material, but artists and free-speech advocates warn they can stifle India's rich tradition of political satire.

"Meta platforms have been restricting the reach of my cartoons for some years," Acharya told the BBC. "But when my entire profile was restricted in India, I was a little sad."

He wrote to Meta, Instagram's parent company, but received no reply. He says he was preparing to go to court when his account became accessible again in early October, only to be blocked again earlier this week for three days.

In a statement, Meta told the BBC that it may temporarily restrict accounts to comply with India's IT Rules but did not explain the specific reasons for restricting Acharya's account or Manjul's post.

Critics say the restrictions come as humour and satire play an increasingly visible role in political dissent in India, particularly among younger people.

Memes and Gen-Z humour helped fuel protests over education and jobs in July, which led to the resignation of India's education minister. Online debate has also intensified over a controversial revision of voter rolls that removed 130 million names.

The political significance of social media has not been lost on the government. Prime Minister Narendra Modi's Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) has urged minister s to strengthen their online presence and connect with younger audiences.

At the same time, technology policy expert Prateek Waghre says the government is increasingly using legal orders to regulate online content.

The Indian Express reported , external that government agencies sent nearly 195,000 blocking and content-restriction orders to platforms including Instagram, Facebook and YouTube between March and July through the federal government's Sahyog portal.

The figures, obtained through a right-to-information request, do not show how many posts were ultimately restricted or removed. The BBC has not seen the original response.

Waghre says that some platforms, particularly Meta, "seem more willing to comply", he says, while X appears more willing to push back. But limited public data makes comparisons difficult. Meta declined to comment on his assessment.

The government has also reportedly sought greater scrutiny of how social media platforms recommend content.

Earlier this week, several media outlets reported , external that authorities had asked Meta to ensure its systems did not steer users towards "a single or limited set of narratives" and strengthen checks on content that could "cause public disorder or incite violence".

The BBC has sought comment from India's IT ministry on the restrictions and reported instructions to Meta but has not received a response.

Of course, political satire has a long history in India - as do attempts to curb it.

Cartoons have been a fixture of Indian journalism since independence, with RK Laxman 's Common Man becoming one of its most recognisable characters.

But cartoonists have also faced censorship. During the Emergency in the 1970s, when civil liberties were suspended and the press was tightly controlled, Abu Abraham continued drawing, even as dozens of his cartoons were stamped "not passed by censors".

In 2012, cartoonist Aseem Trived i was arrested on sedition charges over cartoons allegedly mocking the Indian constitution. The charges were later dropped.

Today, concerns about restrictions on political expression extend beyond cartoonists. India ranks 157th in Reporters Without Borders' World Press Freedom Index, while critics accuse the government of putting growing pressure on independent media. The government rejects the criticism, saying India's media remains free and vibrant.

Comedians have also faced controversy over political satire. Kunal Kamra , known for his jokes about Prime Minister Narendra Modi and his party, has faced threats, cancelled shows and legal action.

For cartoonists, however, challenging those in power is central to their work.

"We are among the default opposition," says Sandeep Adhwaryu, a cartoonist at a leading Indian newspaper.

"The nature of the craft is to oppose," he says, adding that cartoonists, like journalists, must question whoever holds power.

Acharya says he has followed that principle throughout his career. Before 2014, many of his cartoons targeted the Congress-led government and were shared by BJP leaders.

"I never faced official restrictions on my cartoons during the previous governments, though there would be some trolling occasionally," he says.

Now, with the BJP in power, much of his satire is directed at Modi's government.

Social media has allowed independent cartoonists like Acharya to reach audiences without relying on newspapers or other traditional outlets.

"We are not associated with newspapers or any mainstream media. That's why we can draw," says Manjul.

But that freedom comes with a new vulnerability - dependence on platforms that can restrict their work or cut off access to their audiences.

No one knows this better than Rachita Taneja, the creator of the hugely popular Instagram comic Sanitary Panels.

"My career would not have existed without the internet," she told the BBC. Yet she describes social media as a double-edged sword.

"At the end of the day it's a for-profit endeavour that answers to advertisers," she says.

Taneja says that Meta's compliance with Indian government requests reflects the company's commercial priorities rather than concern for users' rights. Meta declined to comment.

Even cartoonists working in traditional newsrooms face pressure. Adhwaryu says artists may soften captions, avoid certain subjects or think twice before submitting a cartoon. Over time, he says, such self-censorship can become normalised, even without explicit instructions.

When Acharya's Instagram account was first restricted, Taneja drew a stick-figure cartoon in solidarity. "Seeing people on the front lines creating communities, protesting, running campaigns, tirelessly fighting for their own rights and the rights of others is what keeps me going," she says.

Adhwaryu believes satire will continue to adapt. He compares cartoons and humour to a "shape-shifting virus".

"It keeps mutating in response to its environment," he says. "It will find its way."

items.title: Celebrations in Serbia after veteran ruler Vučić loses election to student-led protest movement
items.summary: The populist right-wing leader of 12 years says it is "clear" his party has lost the vote billed as a referendum on the country's future.
items.content:
Serbia's long-standing leader Aleksandar Vučić has admitted defeat to the student-led protest movement in snap parliamentary elections.

"We still do not have final results... it is clear that we have lost these elections," the right-wing populist leader said as he conceded late on Sunday.

Preliminary figures from Serbia's election commission indicated a record high turnout, which commentators had suggested would favour the student movement. Celebrations erupted after Vučić conceded.

Vučić called the snap elections after two years of protests triggered by the collapse of a train station canopy in the city of Novi Sad, which killed 16 and was seen as emblematic of corruption and negligence.

Vučić had spent two terms as president and could not seek a third term, so was leading his Serbian Progressive Party (SNS) with the aim of returning to the post of prime minister, which he left in 2017.

The Student List's lead candidate Ilija Srdanović told BBC Serbian: "This will be a free state."

He said the anti-corruption movement, which had attracted anti-government voters across Serbia, hoped to "free the country from tyranny".

There were celebrations on the streets of the city, with people dancing and chanting "victory", cars honking, and fireworks set off. "Serbia is free," one student told the BBC. "It's a miracle."

During a celebration speech, Student List candidate Radomir Saicic said Serbians had shown "no obstacle was greater than their will", Reuters reported. "No force can forever overpower a people who have decided to take their destiny into their own hands," he added.

Amid scenes of people dancing in the streets Belgrade, Selena Lebovic said the result was "really fabulous".

"We are all crying, and what to say. We couldn't believe that it would be so easy," she told Reuters.

Vučić made his announcement at the headquarters of his Serbian Progressive Party (SNS) in the capital Belgrade.

The centre of Novi Sad - the northern city that triggered the student-led protests - was crowded. "Everything is going to get better now," David Vasić, one of those celebrating, told the BBC Serbian.

The Student List - which has no obvious leaders and whose members are not used to politics - had attracted anti-government voters across Serbia.

It decided to field candidates to the 250-member parliament from across Serbian society including doctors, actors, academics and sports personalities.

The anti-corruption movement campaigned on a manifesto that included purging officials who broke rules cracking down on protesters, stopping party loyalists from leading public enterprises, and freeing the public broadcaster of political control.

Vučić, who backs Serbia's candidacy for the European Union while refusing to impose sanctions on Russia over its full-scale invasion of Ukraine, had pledged to increase pensions and public sector salaries, and investment in state healthcare.

Preliminary figures provided by Serbia's election commission suggested a record high turnout, with 64.9% having cast their vote by 18:00 local time (17:00 GMT), two hours before polls were set to close.

Earlier in the day, long queues were seen outside polling stations in cities and towns across Serbia.

This was also the case outside booths in a number of countries with sizeable Serbian communities - including Slovenia's capital Ljubljana, Germany's Munich, and Los Angeles and Chicago in the US.

In France, Serbian voters waited in line in heavy rain in Paris.

The election was held amid high tensions across Serbia, with police sealing off streets around the Republic Electoral Commission (RIK) in Belgrade.

Joy and disbelief on Serbian streets as Vučić concedes election defeat

items.title: Removing Next.js Got My Blog to 100 on Every Lighthouse Category
items.summary: Article URL: https://korindiehacker.bloffy.blog/en/removing-nextjs-got-my-blog-to-100-on-every-lighthouse-category Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50237712 Points: 108 # Comments: 63
items.content:
My blog just scored a perfect 100 on every Lighthouse category. I love blogging. I wanted to build a blog that’s light, fast, free of clutter, able to run multiple blogs, and fully accessible on top of that. And finally, at long last, I’ve more or less pulled it off. It was quite a tedious process. Ugh… and I even had to remove Next.js, the framework I’d been using most. It was far, far more painful than I expected. I’d like to share the journey of improving performance while building this blog.

When you think of blogs, a few names come to mind. Medium, Blogger, Ghost… But none of them satisfied me. Medium and Blogger are bloated with features, and their actual performance wasn’t satisfying either.

Hmm…… And there was another problem: it’s a hassle to work directly with the markup and raw code we all love (Markdown, HTML, CSS).

For the record, all performance measurements were taken with pagespeed.web.dev .

Of course, there are plenty of alternatives: WordPress, Ghost, Hugo. I didn’t like WordPress’s plugin hell. Ghost has to be self-hosted (there’s ghost.org too, but it’s way too expensive…), and every version upgrade broke something in the editor, so keeping it up to date was a chore. Hugo is the best of the bunch, but in the end, setting it up is still a hassle. Looking back, I guess what I really wanted was SaaS.

The one I liked most was Bear Blog. Great performance. I love its product philosophy, too. But its extreme minimalism was a downside for me. The editor UX didn’t work for me, either.

If it at least let me add AdSense and attach images for free, I probably would’ve just used Bear Blog.

As fast as Bear Blog, but with a bit more functionality and better usability. That’s the blog I wanted to build. Oh, and if you’re curious, you can check it out at bloffy.co .

Anyway. Enough about me. Let me share how I actually improved the performance.

It goes without saying that caching is essential. Get caching right and performance improves dramatically. And Next.js makes caching really convenient. There’s ISR , and it also extends fetch with a next option for caching . Handy. Using these well alone gets you a long way on performance.

Unfortunately, though, our site can be reached from anywhere in the world. Why is that unfortunate? Within the same region, caching makes things fast, but visitors from other regions still end up eating the network latency.

Yes. That’s why we use a CDN. And if you deploy a Next.js app to Vercel, you get a CDN out of the box. I don’t dislike Vercel; it’s incredibly convenient. But the Pro plan is pricey right from the start, there’s the serverless cold start problem, and the dependency on the Vercel ecosystem isn’t something you can ignore either.

So why not use a different CDN service? Cloudflare, for example. I honestly think Cloudflare is a genuinely nice company. You can run large-scale infrastructure and most apps on it for free. But then I figured I didn’t really need Next.js’s caching anymore. Having to invalidate two caches every time I publish a post makes things a pain to manage.

In short, for a static website, I figured a CDN alone is enough. And that’s reason number one why I didn’t need Next.js.

Images these days run over 10MB. Serve those on the web as-is and your performance will go completely off the rails.

Optimizing images is quite a hassle. You have to resize per device, compress, and then handle the CDN on top of that. On a previous project, I had a serverless function (AWS Lambda) compress and resize images whenever one landed in storage (S3), and I put CloudFront in front as the CDN. It was a pretty reasonable setup for tailoring things exactly the way I wanted. But it’s also a setup that needs a fair amount of upkeep.

So this time I went with Cloudflare’s Image Transformations . Even on the free tier you get 5,000 images, so I use it without a second thought.

At this point I sound like a Cloudflare sales rep. I’m just an ordinary solo developer.

Pretty high scores. But this isn’t enough. We want 100. A clean, no-asterisks 100. So I dug into what the problem was.

It said a substantial amount of legacy JavaScript was found, and it wasn’t code I wrote. It came from the framework runtime that Next.js ships in its bundle.

But this page is a static page with zero interaction. Every page is pre-rendered with ISR, and I thought I’d followed the Next.js guidelines well. So as an experiment, I ripped out every client component the app had, left only server components, and measured again. The score didn’t budge.

At first I suspected hydration , but once I dug in, the problem wasn’t hydration alone. The cause was the client runtime that Next.js always ships, even for static pages. Even with only server components, the runtime chunks, hydration, and the RSC payload for the router all stay. That’s because next/link and next/image are themselves client components ( 'use client' ), so having just those two is enough to pull in the runtime and trigger hydration.

So what if I strip out next/link and next/image too? The App Router’s own runtime, the router and error boundaries, still remains. There’s no official way to get it down to zero; the only option was a hack: stripping the scripts out of the rendered HTML. That’s when it hit me: “If I’m going to do that, why am I even using Next.js?”

You can see that the bulk of the JavaScript is code that isn’t needed. Unused code alone comes to 230,460 bytes. That’s not good. Most static websites don’t need JavaScript at all. Unused JavaScript is needed even less.

This is where I really agonized. Is dropping Next.js for the sake of 100 points the right call? I’d spent a lot of time building the public-facing web app.

In the end, for the quality of the blog (even if it’s just 5 points), I decided to rip Next.js out entirely. My judgment was that I wouldn’t need Next.js’s excess features in the long run either. I considered going fully vanilla, but I didn’t want to give up the productivity and infrastructure benefits of a framework. I needed to find the right one.

I chose Hono . I liked its technical philosophy. “Fast and simple” was exactly the solution I needed most, and JSX support was a bonus. The migration cost didn’t look too big, either.

Tada. And just like that, 100 across the board. Go ahead and run the very page you’re reading right now through pagespeed.web.dev .

There’s no JavaScript, and unused code dropped sharply to 407 bytes. As a bonus, build time went down by about 40% too.

Oh, why is SEO at 69? That site was built for testing, and it deliberately blocks search indexing. That’s why it’s 69.

By the way, if you score 100 on everything in DevTools, Lighthouse actually sets off fireworks for you. 🎉🎉

The long task that runs before anything is rendered on screen took 309.3ms on Next.js, and when I built the same page with Hono, it took 68.01ms. That’s roughly a 78% improvement.

Is a JS payload, hydration included, really doing a static site any good? I don’t think so. It leaves behind unnecessary JavaScript, so in most cases I think it’s simply not needed.

That said, for an interaction-heavy app, I think Next.js can be a great framework. In fact, the management app for this very blog is built with Next.js!

P.S. This blog runs on Bloffy, the blogging platform I’m building. If you want a blog that scores like this without the setup, you can try it at bloffy.co .

items.title: iRobot è così sicura dei suoi Roomba da farteli provare a casa per 30 giorni
items.summary: Il Roomba si porta a casa, si mette al lavoro sui propri pavimenti e, se non convince, si restituisce entro 30 giorni con il rimborso del prezzo pagato. Vale anche sui modelli in offerta ... Leggi tutto
items.content:
Un robot aspirapolvere si sceglie leggendo le schede, ma si giudica solo a casa propria, tra il divano e il tappeto del soggiorno. Per questo iRobot ha deciso di togliere di mezzo il dubbio. Chi compra un Roomba ha 30 giorni per provarlo nella vita di tutti i giorni e, se non lo convince, lo restituisce e riceve indietro i soldi. Il programma si chiama Soddisfatti o Rimborsati e sarà attivo fino al 31 marzo 2027 .

Dietro c'è un ragionamento semplice. Un'azienda propone una prova così lunga solo quando è convinta che, dopo un mese di pulizie, il robot si sarà guadagnato il suo posto in casa.

Passerà sotto il letto? E sul tappeto a pelo lungo si arrampicherà o rimarrà impigliato? Riuscirà a stare dietro al pelo del gatto che cambia stagione? Come laverà il mio parquet? Sono le domande che si fa chiunque stia per comprare un robot , e nessuna scheda tecnica può rispondere per una casa che non conosce.

Trenta giorni bastano per scoprirlo . In pochissimo tempo un Roomba impara la pianta dell'appartamento e si abitua a soglie e bordi dei tappeti, passando dal parquet del soggiorno alle piastrelle del bagno. Chi ha animali lo vede al lavoro nei giorni normali, quelli in cui il pelo si accumula negli angoli e sotto i mobili. E chi vuole avere sempre un pavimento lavato di fresco potrà testare anche le capacità di lavare e asciugare il rullo del robot sulla base AutoWash dei modelli che la prevedono, per evitare muffe e cattivi odori.

È anche il modo migliore per apprezzare i Roomba più recenti . Il 115 e i Plus 415, 515 e 575 hanno un profilo fino al 21% più sottile del Roomba Plus 505. Se sulla carta è un numero, sotto il proprio divano diventa la polvere che finalmente sparisce.

Il meccanismo è pensato per non complicare la vita a chi compra.

1. Si acquista il Roomba da un qualunque rivenditore, in negozio oppure online.

2. Entro 10 giorni dall'acquisto lo si registra su irobot.it , caricando lo scontrino o la conferma d'ordine.

3. Si usa il robot in casa , come si farebbe con qualunque elettrodomestico appena comprato.

4. Se non convince, entro 30 giorni dall'acquisto si chiede il reso dalla propria area riservata . Un corriere passa a ritirarlo senza costi e il prezzo pagato torna con un bonifico.

L'unica accortezza è conservare la scatola originale e lo scontrino , perché il Roomba torna indietro completo, come è arrivato.

La prova vale anche quando il Roomba si compra in promozione. Chi approfitta di uno sconto da un rivenditore conserva i suoi 30 giorni e, in caso di reso, riceve indietro quanto ha effettivamente pagato. Restano fuori soltanto i Roomba ottenuti come omaggio, per esempio in un'offerta 3x2, o vinti come premio di un concorso.

Con le offerte di ottobre ancora in corso , è il momento più conveniente per mettere un Roomba alla prova .

Sul negozio ufficiale di iRobot i 30 giorni ci sono già "di serie", per ogni acquisto . Chi ordina da irobot.it non deve registrarsi al programma. Se il robot non lo convince, lo restituisce con la normale procedura di reso del sito, entro 30 giorni dalla consegna.

Il programma non si limita a qualche modello di punta. Comprende i Roomba d'ingresso come il 115 , i Plus delle serie 400, 500 e 600, i Max delle serie 700 e 800, fino al Mini Combo. Valgono anche le versioni proposte su Amazon. L'unica condizione è che il robot sia nuovo e distribuito in Italia da Nital, con il Sigillo di Garanzia Ufficiale Italia sulla confezione.

Se ci si vuole affidare a punti vendita fisici, il rivenditore più vicino si trova con la ricerca dei rivenditori di iRobot , mentre la pagina del programma spiega come registrarsi . Per l'elenco completo dei modelli e tutte le condizioni del rimborso conviene leggere il regolamento .

items.title: Steal My Bitcoin CTF PoC
items.summary: Article URL: https://github.com/KillaBoi/StealMyBitcoin-PoC Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50237379 Points: 86 # Comments: 14
items.content:
One live PHP callback against the Steal My Bitcoin challenge, start to finish, in a single standard-library Python file.

This README explains stealmybitcoin_poc.py , a single-file Python reproduction of the request sequence used in my Steal My Bitcoin CTF run. It uses only Python's standard library. The script builds the requests itself, checks each leak before moving on, and records the HTTP bytes from a new run.

This can probably be done easier without all the extra debug crap and as in my John Hammond video about the Steam Local Privilege Escalation I discovered, you could probably clean up this ugly PoC.

⚠️ Honestly please clean it up or make your own better version that isn't crumpled by Sol. ⚠️

Everything below is written against the Docker lab , not the live challenge. The lab is a local Alpine PHP 8.4.26 CLI server behind nginx, which is the same build and worker model the offsets were calibrated on. Stand it up in a minute and the whole chain runs end to end on your own machine. The live run that actually solved the challenge is kept as a historical note at the bottom .

Why two addresses? The OS randomizes where PHP's code and heap land, independently. The heap leak tells the script where to put the forged structure, the code leak tells it where the function it wants to call actually lives. Addresses from an earlier worker or an earlier run are not safe substitutes, and every time I tried it the attempt just failed.

The offsets in this PoC are calibrated for Alpine PHP 8.4.26 running the built-in CLI server with four workers . The lab reproduces exactly that, behind nginx, on loopback.

The build matters more than the version string. A Debian php:8.4.26-fpm stack reports the same PHP/8.4.26 but has a different binary layout, so the code-pointer fingerprint will never match and the run aborts at the code-leak stage. Use the Alpine image below.

public/php-version.php (the health endpoint, and the only page the PoC needs)

print-flag (stand-in for the challenge binary, must be executable)

The PID varies with whichever worker answers, and that is fine. The version line is the part the PoC checks.

Tear it down with docker rm -f ctf-cross-nginx ctf-cross-php && docker network rm ctf-cross-net .

On Windows, run those docker run commands from PowerShell, or replace $PWD with a full drive path like C:/lab . In Git Bash $PWD expands to an MSYS path such as /tmp/... , which Docker Desktop resolves inside its own VM. The bind mounts then silently create empty directories where nginx.conf and print-flag should be, and the containers come up broken.

A couple of notes on that recipe. The image is the fpm tag but the container runs php -S , so the SAPI is cli-server , which is what the calibration was measured against. PHP_CLI_SERVER_WORKERS=4 is what gives the leak stages more than one worker to race for. My own lab harness also passed --cap-add SYS_PTRACE --security-opt seccomp=unconfined so it could attach a tracer to the workers; the PoC itself never does that, so those are left out above.

Python 3.11 or newer, standard library only, nothing to install:

Run it with no arguments and it prints its help and exits without touching the network.

Note the low 21 bits of that zval_ptr_dtor value: 0x112930 , exactly the fingerprint the script expects from this Alpine build. That is the check that rejects a mismatched image.

The PHP fatal, then the nonce this run generated, then id , then the hash of the binary it resolved, then the dummy flag. Exit status is 0 on a verified run and 1 on anything else.

The producer deliberately walks PHP into its memory limit. Only run this somewhere that behaviour is authorized. The script will only talk to the challenge endpoint or a loopback lab URL, and anything else aborts before a packet goes out.

One run means one health GET, up to two leak batches, and at most one final request. No looping, no retries. Every multipart body stays under 1 MiB, though each leak batch pipelines nine separate requests down one connection.

That is 20 HTTP requests at most : one health check, nine per leak batch, one final request. All eight consumers in a batch go out before the first response is read, which helps the timing, but it also means you cannot pull them back if the producer fails. A failed or malformed batch stops the next stage.

The fatal you want says PHP exhausted its 128 MiB memory limit. What you are actually after is the stale state this particular failure leaves behind in a worker.

On its own, a memory-limit fatal or an nginx 502 proves nothing about an address leak or code execution.

The script checks the pointer's range and its low 21 bits, 0x112930 . That is the page offset of the symbol in the Alpine PHP 8.4.26 image, and ASLR does not move it. Treat it as a fingerprint, not as proof the remote executable is byte for byte the same thing. For this layout, zif_system works out as:

Both leaks have to come from the current invocation. The script will not load historical pointer values into a live attempt.

The final POST parks a 384-byte forged HashTable in a multipart field I control. That structure overlaps a fake call frame and a fake zend_string holding the command. A 276-byte primer supplies a pointer into the controlled region, then a long form-field name drives another memory-limit failure. In the cleanup path, PHP reads the forged table's pDestructor as zif_system and hands it the string argument.

The target address uses a distance measured in the four-worker Alpine setup:

That distance depends on the worker and the allocation layout. Change the image, the memory configuration, or the worker count and this falls over even though the PHP version still reads 8.4.26.

The command that originally worked just ran print-flag once. This version prints a fresh random nonce, the output of id (UID and GID), and the SHA-256 of the resolved print-flag binary before invoking print-flag once. It hunts down the active accepted socket under /proc/self/fd so the output actually reaches the HTTP response. Ordinary process stdout got me nothing.

Every run drops a new poc-run- directory, unless --output-dir points at a new one. Everything is written before it is validated, so a run that aborts halfway still leaves usable evidence. The files worth opening:

execution_proof_verified: true means the final response came back HTTP 200 carrying the fresh nonce, an id result, and a SHA-256 line for print-flag .

Against the real challenge a run directory can contain a live private key. Publish this source file, not a run's output.

The script makes no claim about whether a returned WIF controls the advertised Bitcoin address. A checksum-valid WIF only tells you the string encodes a private key properly. Deriving the address and comparing it is a separate job.

Both leak stages are races against three other workers, so a single run is not expected to succeed every time. Ten consecutive runs against the lab described above, with no retries and nothing else talking to the container:

So roughly seven runs in ten. Worth knowing that both leaks are stable once a container is up: every run against the same container returned the same zend_heap_base and the same zval_ptr_dtor , because the workers persist and ASLR is per process, not per request. What varies between runs is purely which worker answers which pipelined consumer.

The two failures are worth recognising, because they look nothing alike:

Callback misses. Both leaks succeed, the final POST returns HTTP 200, and the body is only the memory-limit fatal with none of the three markers. The forged table did not land where cleanup read it:

Neither case is a partial success, and neither is retried automatically. Just run it again.

Worth being straight about the gaps. The original run never captured its full outgoing HTTP request or the response headers. The complete request was reconstructed afterwards from the builders and whatever metadata was left over, and a matching hash would not promote that into an original wire capture. I never pulled the remote PHP ELF or the print-flag binary, they were simply executed, as noted on the challenge website. The one WIF I recovered did not derive the prize address shown on the saved homepage at the time. That was a mistake on the creator's side, and it was acknowledged over email.

It is laid out in attack order and the section banners match the four stages above:

Every tuned number lives in the calibration block at the top or in the STAGES table, so that is the place to look when something needs re-measuring against a different build.

items.title: Guerra in Iran, le news di oggi. Domani Israele al voto, Trump: “Bibi guerriero eccezionale”
items.summary: Il presidente degli Stati Uniti ha esortato gli israeliani a votare per il primo ministro Benjamin Netanyahu citando la guerra tra Stati Uniti e Israele contro l'Iran come esempio di "vittoria condivisa".
items.content:
Il primo ministro israeliano Benjamin Netanyahu ha dichiarato domenica di aver istruito l'agenzia di intelligence israeliana Mossad e l'esercito a rovesciare il governo iraniano, avvertendo che Teheran potrebbe ancora rappresentare una minaccia nucleare nonostante i precedenti raid militari.

Thrall: “Per i diritti dei palestinesi non ci sarà il cambiamento”

Cnn: “Forze armate Usa pronte ad operazioni su vasta scala in Iran entro 96 ore dall’ordine di Trump”

Cnn: “Forze armate Usa pronte ad operazioni su vasta scala in Iran entro 96 ore dall’ordine di Trump”

Le forze americane in Medio Oriente sono pronte a lanciare nuove operazioni militari contro l' Iran , potenzialmente su vasta scala, "entro 96 ore dal ricevimento" di un ordine del presidente Donald Trump . Lo riporta la Cnn , citando due funzionari statunitensi. Le nuove operazioni andrebbero probabilmente oltre il "taglio dell'erba", cioè i raid mirati contro radar, lanciatori e altre infrastrutture che Teheran riesce a ricostruire in fretta. Raid di questo tipo sono stati condotti da quando, all'inizio dell'anno, Trump ha interrotto le operazioni di combattimento su larga scala. "Sarà un grande sforzo", ha detto uno dei funzionari all'emittente. La valutazione è condivisa da altri funzionari, in servizio e in pensione, a conoscenza della pianificazione militare. Alcuni di loro ritengono che la questione non sia se Trump darà il via libera, ma quando.

Giordania, arrestate tre persone per l’attacco alla chiesa greco-ortodossa nel villaggio di Hammoud

Le forze di sicurezza giordane hanno arrestato tre persone in relazione all'attacco senza precedenti a una chiesa greco-ortodossa, che ha causato nove morti e 25 feriti. Re Abdullah II , che ha incontrato le vittime dopo l'attacco, aveva dichiarato, durante una riunione del Consiglio di Sicurezza Nazionale, che "la sicurezza dei giordani è una linea rossa e la mano della giustizia raggiungerà ogni terrorista".

Il presidente degli Stati Uniti Donald Trump ha invitato gli israeliani a votare per il primo ministro Netanyahu alle prossime elezioni, citando la guerra israelo-americana contro l'Iran come esempio di “vittoria condivisa”. “Quando andate alle urne, ricordatevi che Bibi è stato un primo ministro guerriero eccezionale”, ha scritto Trump sulla sua piattaforma Truth Social, riferendosi a Netanyahu con il suo soprannome.

items.title: Data centre debate heats up ahead of US midterms - here's what you need to know
items.summary: Data centres are the lifeblood of our digital world, but there are growing concerns about their environmental impact. The BBC explores their rise in charts.
items.content:
Until a few years ago many of us may have been blissfully unaware of what a data centre was.

These giant, warehouse-like buildings power virtually all our internet activity, from our web searches and emails to movie downloads and online banking.

They are at the heart of the AI boom, housing the advanced computer chips and servers needed to run services like ChatGPT and Claude.

But the speed at which they're growing, the enormous amount of electricity they consume and concerns about their environmental impact are fuelling a public backlash around the world.

In the US, they've become a huge issue ahead of the midterm elections on 3 November, with both Republicans and opposition Democrats coming out against their development.

It's putting opponents of data centre expansion on a collision course with US President Donald Trump, who has dismissed the pushback as a "sick conspiracy", even as public anger grows.

Here's what you need to know about the data centre boom, and why opposition is growing.

There are about 12,250 data centres around the world, according to Data Center Map , external , a company that tracks both operational and pre-operational sites.

That's up sharply from 2021, when there were around 8,000 , external operational sites.

As the chart below shows, data centres are most densely clustered in the US which has 4,767 sites. It is followed by Europe, where the UK and Germany lead.

Data centres have typically been located near to cities where it's easier to access high voltage power lines or water resources for cooling. But as they get bigger, more are being built in rural areas.

But when it comes to actual capacity, the US is ahead by a much larger margin, with China in second place and Europe lagging far behind.

This gap is set to widen in the coming years, leading some to warn Europe risks missing out on the potential economic benefits of the AI boom , external .

Data centres vary wildly in size, ranging from ones that fit inside a garden shed to others covering vast expanses of land.

The world's largest operational data centre is widely reported to be one run by China Telecom in Hohhot, Inner Mongolia, covering an area of approximately one million square metres (10.7 million sq ft). That is equivalent to about 140 Fifa football pitches.

However, much larger sites are under construction as the graphic below shows.

All these sites are being built exclusively to provide the immense computing power needed to run AI services.

For instance, Colossus 2, which is part of the wider Colossus campus, will house hundreds of thousands of advanced AI chips made by tech giant Nvidia.

It will also be used to train xAI's chatbot Grok. Elon Musk's company will use 41 methane gas turbines to help power the site, which activists say could "significantly increase" local air pollution , external . Local regulators say the turbines will meet air quality standards.

The pressure data centres put on local resources has sparked increasing concern. These facilities can use significant amounts of water to cool their systems, which could lead to water shortages , some experts say.

Data centres worldwide are also thought to consume more electricity than the whole of France, as the chart below shows.

This growing hunger for power is driving up carbon emissions, analysis shows , while putting pressure on local grids, which some fear could push up energy prices .

With others worried about the noise data centres make and the space they take up, a public backlash is gathering steam.

Some 16 US states have proposed laws to ban or temporarily block new facilities, and it could be a key issue in November's midterm elections .

Outside the US, opposition to data centres has emerged in countries like Mexico , France, Indonesia and the UK .

But supporters say data centres are critical to national security , and the development of AI.

They also say they are good for the economy , external , attracting investment, generating tax revenue and creating jobs in areas like construction.

A recent report by the Brookings Center , external suggests data centres do create local jobs, although fewer than industry advocates claim.

The type of data centre matters too. So-called hyperscale facilities - massive sites owned and run by tech giants like Amazon and Microsoft - have a bigger positive effect on jobs, it found.

But "colocation" facilities, which lease space to remote tenants without a local presence, brought fewer benefits.

As the debate over their merits intensifies, the data centre rollout continues.

This year, the tech industry is expected to spend a combined $765bn , external ($544bn) on AI infrastructure in 2026, with this topping $1tn next year.

But as concerns about the environmental impact grow, the tech industry is exploring alternatives.

One idea is to put data centres in space , external or on the Moon , where they could harness abundant solar energy.

Others predict that more AI processing could eventually be carried out by the hardware already inside our computers and smartphones , reducing the need for vast data centres altogether.

Additional reporting and design by Erwan Rivault, Matt Faraci and Dominic Bailey.

items.title: Rapper Nicki Minaj joins Trump onstage at Michigan rally
items.summary: The Super Bass singer is the latest big name to campaign in Michigan, where a tight Senate race is playing out ahead of the 3 November midterms.
items.content:
Rapper Nicki Minaj said US President Donald Trump has "changed the energy of the country" as she joined him at a Michigan rally to stump for Republicans ahead of the nationwide midterm elections.

"He's given us a future to look forward to," she said, after Trump praised her figure and called her on stage to speak.

Minaj has called herself Trump's "number one fan" despite criticising some of his policies in his first term.

In Michigan, Democratic Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed is locked in a tight race with Republican Mike Rogers with just over a week to go before the midterms. Former President Barack Obama held a rally - one of the first in this cycle - with the Democrat on Saturday.

Democrats are also aggressively hitting the campaign trail, with close elections taking place on 3 November which will decide which party controls Congress for the rest of Trump's presidency.

In his remarks on Sunday, Trump focused on El-Sayed's Muslim faith and background, alleging that he will "invite jihadists" into America if he wins.

El-Sayed has criticised similar remarks by Trump as Islamophobic, saying in an ad to voters last week that the US president "thinks he can use my name and my faith to distract us from the suffering his policies are inflicting on us at the pump, at the grocery store, and at the doctor's office".

In Port Huron on Sunday, Minaj, wearing a gold-coloured Gucci-branded suit, led the crowd in chanting Trump's name, and the names of Republican candidates in Michigan.

"We really need all these great people to be elected, because this is a major turning point for our country," she said.

"She never looked more beautiful," Trump said as she left the stage. "She gets it. She's smart," he added.

Earlier in his speech, Trump praised the rear end of one male Republican candidate before turning the crowd's attention to Minaj.

"By the way, I looked at a beautiful ass before," he segued. "Nicki Minaj. That's hard to miss."

He then asked her to "stand up" as the crowd cheered, and added that he hoped she was not "insulted" by his remark.

The Super Bass singer had accompanied Trump to the state aboard Air Force One. She filmed a video with an aide - which was posted to X -on the president's plane, pretending to be interviewing for the White House press secretary role.

The position is currently open after Katie Zacharia left five days after a shaky public debut.

The Trinidad and Tobago-born rapper has thrown her star power behind Trump a few times before, including on his allegations that Christians face persecution in Nigeria and his "gold card" visa, which offers applicants residency and a path to US citizenship.

Obama attacks Trump as he campaigns for Democrats ahead of midterm elections

items.title: F1: Antonelli vince ad Austin, il Mondiale sempre più vicino
items.summary: Precede Leclerc e Verstappen, in Messico la gara per il titolo
items.content:
Kimi Antonelli vince il Gran Premio degli Usa, ad Austin, e vede avvinarsi sempre più il titolo mondiale. Tutto è rinviato al prossimo Gp di Città del Messico dove all'italiano della Mercedes basterà chiudere tra i primi nove oppure decimo anche se dovesse vincere George Russell. Addirittura potrebbe non fare punti se lo stesso Russell e Lewis Hamilton non dovessero vincere. In classifica Antonelli ha 123 punti di vantaggio su Russell, quando ce ne sono 125 a disposizione.

Ulteriore prova di forza del bolognese che non si accontenta di controllare la gara ma la domina. Il campione 20enne partiva dalla pole position: si impone sulla Ferrari di Charles Leclerc e la Red Bull di Max Verstappen grazie alla strategia Mercedes che sul circuito texano ha previsto un solo cambio di gomme contro i due dei due inseguitori. La vittoria negli States non è però bastata al giovane talento italiano per aggiudicarsi la corona iridata al primo match point in quanto Hamilton e Russell si sono piazzati rispettivamente al quarto e all'ottavo posto, combinazioni difficili da realizzarsi ma che in certi momenti della gara si erano intraviste. "So che siamo molto vicini a vincere il Mondiale, ma vorremmo chiudere in bellezza. Vorremmo vincere altre gare. Speriamo di concludere tutto presto", racconta Kimi dopo la gara. Parte benissimo Antonelli che allunga subito su Verstappen attaccato immediatamente dalle due Ferrari. Leclerc è protagonista di un bel duello con l'olandese che però resiste. Pochi giri ed i commissari sventolano le bandiere gialle per la presenza di detriti in pista. Kimi è sempre al comando e distanzia la Red Bull di Verstappen. Più indietro Russell, già in difficoltà, che viene punito con una penalità di cinque secondi per aver tratto vantaggio da un'uscita di pista. Al 13mo giro Verstappen anticipa il rientro ai box per il cambio gomme. Lo seguono le due Ferrari. Le Mercedes scelgono la sosta unica; stessa tattica anche per la seconda Red Bull guidata da Hadjar. Al 23mo giro rientra Russell che sconta i cinque secondi di penalità e rientra decimo. Al 24mo è il turno di Antonelli: l'italiano rientra terzo. Al 26mo va ai box anche Hadjar. Al 28 giro primo Verstappen seguito da Leclerc, Antonelli e Hamilton; mentre Russell risale all'ottavo posto. Al 32mo secondo pit stop per Verstappen. Leclerc è leader della corsa ma resiste mezzo giro all'attacco di Antonelli che allunga. Al 39mo Hamilton cambia le gomme e rientra sesto. Fa lo stesso Leclerc che rientra quarto. Il ferrarista e Verstappen si lanciano all'inseguimento di Antonelli. Il monegasco fa una serie di giri più veloci ma la Mercedes dell'italiano ha un abbondante vantaggio. Alle spalle del bolognese la McLaren di Norris che deve resistere agli attacchi di Verstappen e Leclerc. Il campione del mondo in carica però deve cedere ai due inseguitori che ingaggiano un duello per il secondo posto. Al 49mo il ferrarista supera l'olandese e si lancia alla disperata rincorsa di Antonelli che, a sette giri dalla bandiera a scacchi ha 13 secondi di vantaggio. L'inseguimento viene anche rallentato da una virtual safety car per l'uscita della Cadillac di Bottas. Gli ultimi chilometri sono una parata per Antonelli e la sua Mercedes. Al traguardo il boato del pubblico statunitense che lo festeggia.

items.title: F-Zero X on Nintendo 3DS
items.summary: Article URL: https://hypnotize.works/gdx-3ds/postmortem/index.html Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50237078 Points: 101 # Comments: 52
items.content:
A post-mortem of porting G-Diffuser, the F-Zero X decompilation, to the Nintendo 3DS — v1.0.0, covering both the original 24-day sprint that put it on a New 3DS at 60 fps in 3D (2026-08-11 to 09-03) and the 43-day second phase that added Old 3DS support, a native renderer, and the Expansion Kit (2026-09-07 to 10-19). One person directed throughout; one long-lived Claude session orchestrated; 147 subagents built the first phase and many more carried the second.

The console went from a black screen to a native-60 stereoscopic racer, then from a New-3DS-only build to a four-way release covering both consoles with and without the 64DD expansion.

The clips and photos below are from v0.9 (2026-09), before DASH replaced the debug console on the bottom screen.

Three released console builds from one source tree, all booting from the HOME menu (.cia) or the homebrew launcher (.3dsx): the base game for Old 3DS / 2DS and for New 3DS / New 2DS XL, and a New 3DS build with the 64DD Expansion Kit (course editor and machine creator, playable with a user-supplied disk image). Every build reads prebaked asset archives from the SD card — no ROM or disk image ever ships with the game.

They play the whole game: Grand Prix, Time Trial, Practice, Death Race, and the machine editor screens, with music and effects on the real DSP, stereoscopic 3D on the slider, a bottom-screen dashboard with three HUD layouts and an idle view outside races, and clean HOME suspend, resume, close, lid sleep and power-off. The New 3DS build keeps the native-60 frame pacing the first phase reached; the Old 3DS build gets to a comparable result by a different route. At v1.0.0, with no ini, both builds default to that same route: the native renderer ( [perf] preset = auto ). The New 3DS's first-phase render-thread/per-draw-stereo path is still built in and reachable with an explicit ini, but is no longer the default — see Frontier and Pushing the boundaries for the two builds compared side by side.

Not originally planned; it ran 09-07 to 10-19, 43 calendar days.

See Agentic workflow for how the second phase was run and Old 3DS for the full campaign, card by card.

items.title: Trieste, pasti ai migranti vietati nel weekend.“Disturbano l’aperitivo”
items.summary: Per motivi di decoro, la questura permette l’attività umanitaria in tempi contingentati. Linea d’ombra: “Ci hanno lasciato solo l’ora d’aria”. Le associazioni: “Ai migranti si impedisce per mesi di presentare richiesta asilo, laboratorio di repressione che crea illegalità”
items.content:
Quando su Trieste scende la sera, non sono i vecchi lampioni asburgici ma le luci blu delle camionette a illuminare piazza Libertà. Davanti, gli agenti schierati. Sotto la statua della principessa Sissi però non ci sono né presidi, né manifestazioni. Solo ragazzi — faccia smunta e vestiti laceri — che arrivano alla spicciolata e un gruppetto di volontari che smistano coperte e pasti. Per questura e prefettura, un problema di sicurezza che da aprile ha meritato l’impiego di «36 funzionari, 106 operatori dei presidi territoriali e 1740 del reparto mobile» e adesso tempi contingentati. Per ragioni di ordine pubblico, si aiuta dalle 18 alle 20, poi tutti a casa.

Nella città che da tre anni ha visto tornare i militari al valico e da agosto per decreto è “zona di transito e frontiera”, anche la solidarietà è contingentata. Nel weekend, addirittura vietata «per consentire il libero svago» . La destra cittadina e regionale, che scalda i motori in vista delle comunali, applaude. Nulla possono 24mila firme raccolte in pochi giorni. Nulla può il vescovo di Trieste, monsignor Enrico Trevisi, che dopo due settimane di solidarietà contingentata per ordine della questura, con una nota tuona: “L'indifferenza verso chi soffre è una grave malattia che va curata”.

«Ci hanno lasciato l’ora d’aria», mastica amaro Gianandrea Franchi . Professore di storia e filosofia, a 90 anni suonati, in piazza non manca mai. Insieme alla moglie Lorena Fornasir , una decina di anni fa ha fondato l’associazione Linea d’ombra per tendere una mano ai migranti della rotta balcanica. Lo hanno pagato con un’inchiesta finita in un nulla di fatto, l’ostilità della destra istituzionale e il dossieraggio di quella che intossica i social con odio e fake news, ma non hanno mai fatto un passo indietro. Attorno, un nucleo duro di attivisti e poi una rete larga, che tiene insieme gli scout e i centri sociali, la Diaconia valdese, medici e prof volontari, associazioni e ong come Mediterranea e ResQ , si stende fino a gruppi che arrivano da mezzo Nord-Est e dall’Emilia, a turno portano pasti, abiti, braccia «per aiutare», occhi «per testimoniare». Anzi, portavano. Da quando le restrizioni sono iniziate è tutto paralizzato.

«Ogni giorno ci chiedono di tornare, ma non possiamo rischiare che vietino anche questo», dice Veronica , fra le “storiche” di Linea d’ombra, mentre smista giubbotti in una piazza fino a qualche settimana fa animata come una festa di paese e adesso solo crocevia di gente che sussurra, prende una borsa con beni essenziali, si guarda attorno impaurita. Come Hibibi, giovane pm fuggito dall’Afghanistan dopo che i talebani hanno sterminato tutta la sua famiglia. O una coppia nepalese appena arrivata, con lei che zoppica vistosamente. «Dicono di garantire la sicurezza, ma siamo noi a farlo — attacca Lara — Le persone hanno l’abitudine di mangiare, coprirsi. Se non lo trovano qui, proveranno a procurarselo in un altro modo». Magari grazie ai caporali che la presenza di volontari e mediatori aveva allontanato, ora tornati a farsi vedere.

È vero, in città c’è una rete solidale strutturata: dalla mensa della Caritas al centro diurno, dai dormitori all’ambulatorio dei medici di Donk . Dove lo Stato non c’è, la società civile ci mette una pezza. Ma i vuoti sono tanti, gli arrivi in aumento — del 31% censiscono le associazioni e conferma la Slovenia, che protesta per il perdurare della frontiera — le necessità pure. La piazza rimane la prima linea perché lì arrivano tutti: chi transita e chi resta. E per mesi deve vivere da fantasma.

«Trieste è un laboratorio della repressione che crea illegalità», ragiona Gianfranco Schiavone di Ics, Consorzio italiano di solidarietà, fra i pionieri dell’accoglienza diffusa. Dopo l’approvazione del patto Ue, per circa due mesi le nuove procedure , previste per chi arrivi dai “Paesi sicuri” e cerchi di eludere i controlli alle frontiere esterne, sono state applicate anche a afghani, curdi, vulnerabili o chi si è presentato in questura. « Il 98% è stato annullato in tribunale — spiega Schiavone — Adesso c’è una nuova strategia; le persone sono costrette ad aspettare 85-90 giorni prima di poter richiedere asilo. In mano gli rimane solo un invito a presentarsi e rimangono abbandonati in strada ». Non è una registrazione, quindi formalmente non esistono, sul territorio sono illegali e all’accoglienza non hanno diritto. Secondo le associazioni sono circa 130, per più della metà ci sarebbe posto in accoglienza. «Noi abbiamo 74 posti — conferma Schiavone – ma da mesi non mandano nessuno».

I più si arrangiano tra quel che resta dei magazzini del Porto vecchio. Molti sono chiusi con transenne e filo spinato, altri murati, qualcuno però ancora dà riparo a chi aspetta. Le finestre non ci sono più, le scale si sgretolano, ma negli stanzoni strati di coperte diventano letto e un fornelletto basta per un té o un pasto. Barhun è lì da quattro mesi. In Nepal era un attivista, è scappato dopo un violento pestaggio delle forze di sicurezza. Una lunga cicatrice gli attraversa il viso: «Avevo l’appuntamento per chiedere asilo, per tre volte mi hanno mandato via. Non so dove altro andare». Mamun invece è arrivato da poco. «Non potevo pagare e i passeurs mi hanno strappato il passaporto. In questura mi hanno detto che non posso chiedere asilo. Come faccio?». Dalle finestre rotte sibila solo la bora che monta.

items.title: Gli studenti vincono le elezioni in Serbia, lo annuncia lo sconfitto Vucic
items.summary: Studentska lista avrebbe maggioranza assoluta. E in tutto il Paese esplode la festa
items.content:
Gli studenti hanno vinto le elezioni politiche anticipate in Serbia. E in tutto il Paese, in diretta Tv, è esplosa la festa nelle strade. Secondo i risultati ancora provvisori ma che difficilmente possono cambiare in modo sostanziale, hanno ottenuto il 52% dei voti, che conferirebbero 138 dei 250 seggi del Parlamento nazionale contro il 39% ottenuto dalla lista Serbia Unita dell'ex presidente Aleksandar Vučić, che avrebbe così 104 seggi.

Nessun'altra coalizione in lizza, secondo le proiezioni, ha passato la soglia del 3%, se non i piccoli partiti delle minoranze etniche, che non vi sono soggetti. Con una mossa a sorpresa, proprio Vucic è stato il primo ad apparire in diretta Tv su Rts per annunciare che aveva "perso le elezioni", dopo che la sua annunciata apparizione in diretta aveva fatto temere che intendesse comunicare invece la propria vittoria. Vucic, con espressione mesta ma composta, ha detto che gli studenti hanno condotto una campagna elettorale "scorretta e piena di menzogne" e che non farà nessuno sconto dall'opposizione, ma ha riconosciuto "la vittoria degli studenti". In rappresentanza di questi ultimi, il candidato Radomir Sajčić ha detto su Rts che "la Serbia finalmente ha preso il suo destino in mano, con un risultato che premia quasi due anni di lotta". Il primo della lista studentesca, il cardiologo Ilija Srdjanović, ha precisato che il suo Paese ha "voltato la faccia ad un tiranno: Andiamo verso una Serbia migliore". A premiare gli studenti un'affluenza record, che ha sfiorato il 70%, un dato che non si vedeva da almeno 30 anni e che i commentatori già da tempo prevedevano, sostenendo che avrebbe favorito gli studenti. La festa è esplosa mentre, a urne già chiuse, cresceva un clima di tensione nel centro di Belgrado, con ingenti schieramenti di polizia e la temuta presenza di provocatori. Si è trattato di elezioni che l'ex presidente, dimessosi in settembre per raccogliere la sfida studentesca alla testa della lista Serbia Unita, sentiva di poter perdere. Tradendo nervosismo con le dichiarazioni degli ultimi mesi, nelle quali ha insistito nel definire gli studenti "distruttori" e "inaffidabili", "manovrati da potenze straniere" nemiche della Serbia. Lunghissime le file ai seggi ben prima dell'apertura alle 7 del mattino. Gli studenti hanno consigliato i loro elettori di votare presto, mentre da subito è apparsa alta la tensione, palpabile anche nelle strade, legata alla paura che brogli, irregolarità e manipolazioni potessero inficiare una prova elettorale alla quale guardano l'Europa, l'America e anche la Russia. I pronostici della vigilia, a seconda dell'orientamento dei sondaggisti, davano alternativamente avanti Serbia Unita o la Lista Studentesca, che si è preparata meticolosamente alla prova elettorale anche addestrando oltre 16mila rappresentanti di lista e 60mila controllori fuori dai seggi, che hanno affiancato gli oltre 16mila osservatori, fra internazionali e nazionali, presenti sul territorio, fra cui delegazioni dell'Osce, dell'Odihr, del Consiglio d'Europa e del Parlamento europeo. In Serbia non sono ammessi exit poll. Le prime proiezioni molte ore dopo la chiusura dei seggi fornite da alcune delle associazioni e istituti demoscopici che seguono il voto, come CeSid/Ipsos Serbia e Crta, prima che la Commissione elettorale nazionale (Rik) dia i primi risultati concreti, quando i dati dai seggi iniziano ad affluire ai suoi centri di raccolta dati, unendosi ai voti potenziali dei circa 100mila serbi che votano all'estero e alle centinaia di voti potenziali di serbo-bosniaci residenti nella Bosnia-Erzegovina che hanno ricevuto doppia cittadinanza. In lizza per i 250 seggi del parlamento unicamerale serbo, eletti con sistema proporzionale a collegio unico e una soglia del 3%, c'erano 18 liste.
