items.title: Windows 11: ora puoi spostare la barra delle applicazioni dove vuoi (e c'è di più)
items.summary: Nuove opzioni di personalizzazione con gli ultimi aggiornamenti.
items.content:
Con gli ultimi aggiornamenti distribuiti da Microsoft, aumenta il livello di personalizzazione di Windows 11. Nello specifico, i pacchetti rilasciati tra settembre e ottobre per le versioni 26H2, 25H2 e 24H2 del sistema operativo, hanno introdotto nuove funzioni per il touchpad, la rimappatura del tasto Copilot e più libertà nella configurazione del menù Start e della barra delle applicazioni.

MENÙ START MENO AFFOLLATO

Si parte dal menu Start, uno degli elementi di Windows più utilizzati nelle attività quotidiane, che grazie agli ultimi aggiornamenti si arricchisce di nuove opzioni di configurazione. Recandosi nel menù Impostazioni > Personalizzazione > Start è possibile innanzitutto ridimensionare il pannello, scegliendo tra Piccolo, Grande o Predefinito.

Windows ha scelto di fornire un approccio più attento alla privacy, consentendo ora di nascondere il nome e l'immagine del proprio profilo quando si apre il pannello. Una funzione che può rivelarsi utile quando il notebook personale viene utilizzato in luoghi diversi dal proprio ufficio o abitazione.

items.title: Gli scontri più pesanti di sabato sono avvenuti a Bologna
items.summary: Alla fine di un corteo composto soprattutto da ragazzi giovani ci sono state manovre pericolose della polizia e varie vandalizzazioni
items.content:
Fra le città italiane in cui sabato si sono tenute manifestazioni e cortei simili a quelli dello scorso weekend, popolati soprattutto da ragazzi e ragazze, gli scontri più pesanti con le forze dell’ordine sono avvenuti a Bologna.

Dopo un corteo perlopiù pacifico e alcune manovre della polizia, una frangia violenta ha vandalizzato alcune vie nel centro storico. La polizia ha quindi reagito con durezza: a fine giornata i feriti sono stati 17 , e c’è stato un momento di grande tensione quando un manifestante bloccato dai poliziotti è rimasto a terra per diversi minuti, immobile. Alla fine è stato portato in ospedale da un’ambulanza.

Le proteste erano iniziate in maniera piuttosto spontanea in piazza del Nettuno, in centro storico. In molti si aspettavano di conoscere un punto di ritrovo dalla pagina Instagram Movimento 17 ottobre, che non è mai arrivato (sabato mattina uno dei suoi presunti organizzatori è stato fermato e portato alla questura di Milano ). Nel tardo pomeriggio la manifestazione è diventata un corteo, e diverse centinaia di persone si sono incamminate verso la stazione, che in linea d’aria si trova circa un chilometro a nord.

La polizia ha cercato di incanalare il corteo in alcune vie laterali costringendo i manifestanti a fare il giro largo, e ha creato alcuni blocchi sul percorso per arrivare in stazione. I manifestanti sono stati respinti con la forza verso via Marconi, dove la polizia ha continuato a caricare. In un momento in particolare ha provato una manovra a tenaglia, molto pericolosa, caricando l’inizio e la fine del corteo e lanciando lacrimogeni a chi stava in mezzo.

A quel punto diversi manifestanti sono scappati, altri hanno iniziato a scontrarsi con la polizia, che ha provato a disperderli con lacrimogeni e il potente getto di vari idranti.

Alla fine piccoli gruppi di manifestanti si sono effettivamente dispersi in alcune vie del centro, dove hanno iniziato a vandalizzare quello che trovavano: cestini, cassonetti, bici del bikesharing, un distributore di sigarette, la vetrina di un negozio della Nike. È stato assaltato anche un autobus dell’azienda regionale TPER, a cui sono stati spaccati il parabrezza e quasi tutti i vetri laterali.

Negli ultimi tempi a Bologna stanno ormai diventando una normalità sia le vandalizzazioni in centro durante le proteste – la settimana scorsa avevano causato circa 250mila euro di danni , di cui 50mila soltanto ai cantieri del tram – sia la dura repressione della polizia.

Il 20 luglio a Bologna durante una manifestazione per Abderrahim Fakir, l’uomo morto mentre due agenti di polizia lo stavano immobilizzando a terra, la polizia ha usato gas lacrimogeni e getti d’acqua contro un corteo dove c’erano anche bambini e anziani , generando panico in uno spazio angusto e con poche vie di fuga. Nell’ottobre del 2025 sempre a Bologna durante una manifestazione per la Palestina una donna di 33 anni ha perso la vista da un occhio perché colpita da un lacrimogeno lanciato ad altezza persona.

items.title: Sicurezza: la NHTSA propone luci ciano per le auto a guida autonoma
items.summary: La nuova proposta di aggiornamento della norma FMVSS n. 108 introduce indicatori turchese opzionali per i veicoli senza conducente come il Cybercab.
items.content:
La National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) ha presentato una proposta di regolamentazione per riformare la norma di sicurezza federale FMVSS n. 108 sull'illuminazione dei veicoli a motore. La riforma è concepita specificamente per accogliere i veicoli a guida autonoma (ADS) privi di volante, pedali e specchietti tradizionali, come il Cybercab di Tesla. Il tema è di grande attualità, soprattutto dopo l'apertura di un'inchiesta sul servizio robotaxi di Tesla proprio a causa della mancanza di comandi fisici, la cui risposta ufficiale è attesa entro il 30 ottobre.

Luci ciano per i veicoli che viaggiano in modalità autonoma

La novità principale della proposta riguarda l'introduzione opzionale delle luci di segnalazione ADS di colore ciano (turchese), standardizzate secondo le specifiche SAE J578 e SAE J3134. Queste lampade indicano chiaramente che il veicolo sta viaggiando in modalità di guida totalmente autonoma, ossia senza che sia richiesta l'attenzione o la supervisione attiva di un occupante umano a bordo. Per questo motivo, le luci ciano saranno riservate ai sistemi senza conducente e vietate sui veicoli con guida assistita che richiede il monitoraggio umano, come Tesla FSD (Supervised).

Non sarà un obbligo di legge

I costruttori potranno installare da una a due luci ciano sulla parte anteriore, sui lati e sul retro (da quattro a otto lampade totali) ad un'altezza minima di 15 pollici (circa 38 cm) dal suolo. Le luci dovranno rimanere fisse ed attivarsi in modo sincrono. L'adozione rimarrà facoltativa: l'agenzia intende standardizzare il segnale visivo senza imporlo ai produttori, richiamando un sondaggio su oltre 4.400 conducenti e i test condotti da Mercedes-Benz con Drive Pilot in California.

Eliminati alcuni comandi fisici

Oltre all'illuminazione ciano, la proposta abolisce importanti vincoli strutturali per le autovetture prive di comandi manuali. Per i veicoli senza volante o pedali non saranno più richiesti i comandi fisici azionati a mano o a pedale per indicatori di direzione, luci d'emergenza e abbaglianti, né le relative spie sul cruscotto. Il sistema informatico dell'auto gestirà le luci via software, dovendo integrare soltanto una spia di guasto visibile da ogni sedile. La riforma aggiorna inoltre i test dei fari a fascio integrale alla tensione dichiarata dal costruttore anziché a 12,8 V.La bozza, in consultazione pubblica per 30 giorni sul Federal Register, traccia una cornice regolatoria più definita per i robotaxi. Nei prossimi mesi vedremo come evolverà il quadro normativo negli Stati uniti per le auto a guida autonoma.

items.title: Alle elezioni in Serbia stavolta Aleksandar Vučić rischia davvero di perdere
items.summary: Sarebbe la prima volta in dodici anni, e per di più contro un movimento di protesta studentesco: si vota oggi
items.content:
Per la prima volta dopo dodici anni in cui è al potere, alle elezioni parlamentari di domenica in Serbia Aleksandar Vučić rischia di perdere. Vučić è un politico nazionalista e populista che ha governato in modo autoritario, prima come primo ministro e poi come presidente. A fine settembre si è dimesso, ma è stata una decisione di facciata : gli serviva solo per candidarsi a primo ministro e restare al potere, visto che era arrivato al limite di mandati da presidente.

Il suo principale sfidante alle elezioni è il movimento degli studenti delle università, che da quasi due anni protestano contro il governo.

In Serbia ci sono pochissimi sondaggi affidabili, ma ci si aspetta che il Partito Progressista Serbo di Vučić (SNS) e la Lista studentesca siano molto vicini. I seggi chiuderanno alle 20, probabilmente per i primi risultati ci vorranno ore. Per sapere con sicurezza chi ha vinto potrebbe volerci anche molto più tempo.

Sostenitori del movimento degli studenti a Belgrado, il 21 ottobre 2026 (AP/Armin Durgut)

Le elezioni sono il momento culminante di un ampio movimento di protesta iniziato nel novembre del 2024 dopo che 16 persone rimasero uccise nel crollo della tettoia della stazione di Novi Sad, la seconda città più grande della Serbia. Gli studenti accusarono il governo di essere responsabile del crollo: la stazione era stata appena restaurata, ma per gli studenti i lavori erano stati fatti male, per via della corruzione negli appalti pubblici. Bloccarono decine di facoltà e iniziarono enormi manifestazioni antigovernative.

Nonostante moltissime persone appoggino il movimento, vincere le elezioni per gli studenti sarà comunque difficile, perché la Serbia non è un paese libero.

Spillette e adesivi della lista degli studenti a Belgrado il 16 ottobre. La lista studentesca è la numero 3 sulle schede elettorali (AP/Darko Vojinovic)

Vučić e il suo partito controllano gran parte dei giornali e delle televisioni. Finanziano la loro campagna elettorale con risorse pubbliche e fanno pressione sui dipendenti pubblici per votare SNS. Il movimento degli studenti è forte tra i moltissimi cittadini serbi che vivono all’estero, e quindi Vučić ha ostacolato le procedure di voto nei consolati e nelle ambasciate.

Il governo ha anche fatto approvare una regola alla Commissione elettorale che obbliga gli elettori in tutto il mondo a votare seguendo il fuso orario di Belgrado, rendendo più complicato farlo in posti come l’Australia o gli Stati Uniti.

Vučić e gli studenti hanno fatto campagne elettorali diversissime.

Vučić ha insistito molto sul suo ruolo di leader e sulla necessità di assicurare stabilità alla Serbia, e ha rivendicato i buoni risultati ottenuti in termini di crescita economica durante il suo governo. Ha anche alimentato una certa diffidenza nei confronti dei giovani.

Nello spot qui sotto per esempio è un cameriere che prende ordini da una famiglia: il padre chiede autostrade, la nonna pensioni più alte, la mamma più asili, e così via. Poi arriva il turno dei figli, svogliati e maleducati, che chiedono che Vučić se ne vada e che la Serbia entri nell’Unione Europea e nella Nato (entrambe questioni a cui moltissimi serbi si oppongono). Vučić risponde: «La Nato e l’Europa non ce le abbiamo; però abbiamo la pace e la stabilità».

Gli studenti hanno insistito molto soprattutto sulla lotta alla corruzione e hanno cercato di attrarre sostenitori con manifestazioni, lunghe marce e campagne porta a porta. Si differenziano da Vučić anche perché tutta la loro campagna si è svolta senza leader , seguendo decisioni prese di volta in volta dalle assemblee studentesche.

Anche per questo non è chiaro come governeranno se dovessero vincere. In Serbia, proprio come in Italia, chi vince le elezioni può indicare il candidato primo ministro dopo il voto. Gli studenti per ora non hanno fatto nomi, il loro programma ha 11 punti in tutto ed è piuttosto vago.

Sostenitori di Vučić a un evento della sua campagna elettorale, il 16 ottobre 2026 (AP Photo/Darko Vojinovic)

Oltre alla lista dell’SNS e a quella degli studenti ci sono diversi piccoli partiti, come quelli che rappresentano le minoranze e altri dell’opposizione, che potrebbero diventare decisivi per formare una maggioranza dopo il voto. Alcuni hanno deciso di non presentare candidati e hanno chiesto ai propri elettori di sostenere gli studenti, per aumentare le loro possibilità di vittoria.

Vučić insieme al presidente russo Vladimir Putin, nel 2019 (AP/Darko Vojinovic)

Negli anni in cui è stato al potere, Vučić ha detto di voler proseguire l’integrazione della Serbia nell’Unione Europea, ma non ha fatto progressi significativi (è candidata dal 2012). Allo stesso tempo ha mantenuto rapporti molto stretti con la Cina e con la Russia.

In caso di vittoria degli studenti non è chiaro quanto la politica estera della Serbia potrà cambiare.

Gli studenti non hanno mai espresso una posizione chiara sull’ingresso nell’Unione Europea, che è un argomento molto divisivo nel paese. In altri casi hanno sostenuto posizioni in tutto e per tutto identiche a quelle di Vučić. La Serbia ha venduto armi all’Ucraina, però è anche uno dei pochissimi paesi che non hanno approvato sanzioni contro la Russia dopo l’invasione su larga scala dell’Ucraina, nel 2022: gli studenti hanno detto di voler proseguire su questa linea.

Hanno anche detto che non riconosceranno il Kosovo, un’ex provincia della Serbia che si è dichiarata indipendente nel 2008 ma che la stragrande maggioranza dei serbi e praticamente tutti i partiti politici considerano tuttora parte della Serbia.

items.title: È tornata l’ora solare
items.summary: Il vostro smartphone probabilmente se l'è ricordato da solo: voi invece spostate gli orologi indietro di un'ora
items.content:
Nella notte tra sabato 24 e domenica 25 ottobre è tornata l’ora solare. Il cambio dell’ora è avvenuto alle 3 di domenica: gli smartphone e i dispositivi digitali solitamente si adeguano da soli, mentre una volta svegli bisognerà ricordarsi di spostare l’orario dei dispositivi analogici indietro di un’ora.

Da questo fine settimana in poi, insomma, farà buio un’ora prima, mentre ci sarà un’ora in più di luce la mattina presto. Come ogni anno però il passaggio dall’ora legale all’ora solare alimenta il dibattito tra chi vorrebbe che il cambio dell’ora fosse abolito e chi invece ne sostiene la necessità. Di solito c’è però una conseguenza che rende contenti un po’ tutti: quando si passa all’ora solare si dorme un’ora in più.

L’ora solare è in vigore dall’ultimo fine settimana di ottobre fino all’ultimo di marzo, quando tornerà l’ora legale e l’orario andrà avanti di un’ora. Nel 2027 succederà nella notte tra il 27 e il 28 marzo.

L’ora solare sarebbe quella “naturale”, mentre l’ora legale fu introdotta per legge in molti paesi europei durante la Prima guerra mondiale, con l’obiettivo di risparmiare energia, e in Italia fu abolita e reintrodotta diverse volte. Nel 1980 l’allora Comunità Economica Europea, antenata dell’Unione Europea, stabilì un primo coordinamento tra i suoi paesi in questa materia: l’alternanza attuale deriva da una direttiva del 2001.

Sia in Italia che negli altri paesi che adottano questo sistema (cioè la maggior parte dei paesi occidentali) si discute periodicamente sull’opportunità di cambiare l’ora e sull’ipotesi che la sua adozione porti effettivamente a uno stato di stress temporaneo causato dallo spostamento dei propri ritmi biologici. Alla fine del 2025 per esempio il governo spagnolo di Pedro Sánchez si è mosso nelle istituzioni europee per riproporre di abolire il passaggio dall’ora solare all’ora legale e viceversa, riaprendo così un dibattito annoso. Finora però non è cambiato niente.

Tra i paesi che non fanno il cambio dell’ora ci sono la Russia, l’Argentina, l’India e parte dell’Australia.

items.title: Israel to close West Bank crossings on election day as crackdown escalates
items.summary: The Israeli Defense Forces announces restrictions on the movement of Palestinian workers in the run-up to Tuesday's election.
items.content:
All West Bank land crossings will be closed during Tuesday's election in Israel, the country's military says, and Palestinian workers will be barred from entering all settlements.

The restrictions come amid a crackdown in the occupied West Bank after Palestinian gunmen killed two Israeli soldiers in the territory.

The Israel Defense Forces announced a "ban on the entry and exit of Palestinian workers throughout Judea and Samaria and the Jordan Valley, including industrial zones, as well as the closure of all land crossings" on Tuesday.

It said most workers would also be barred from settlements from Sunday, with the exception of industrial zones and a limited number of other areas.

Before the Hamas-led October 7, 2023 attack on Israel, more than 100,000 Palestinian workers were permitted to enter Israel. Since then only a small fraction have had their permits restored.

Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu announced a major operation on Friday in response to the killing of two Israeli soldiers by two Palestinian gunmen in an attack on a checkpoint. Three other Israeli soldiers were injured, and the gunmen were also killed.

The Israeli military have been demolishing homes and businesses in the city of Hebron, with hundreds of families having been displaced .

Israeli Defence Minister Israel Katz said about 2,000 residents had been displaced by the operation, which has led to at least one whole street appearing to have been flattened, according to footage shared online.

Even before the entry and exit bans on workers were announced by the IDF on Sunday, the military had cordoned off the city, heavily restricting the movement of its 200,000 residents.

It is common for Israeli forces to demolish the homes of Palestinians who are suspected of carrying out attacks on Israelis in the West Bank - a practice Israeli rights groups have criticised as collective punishment.

Friday's shooting came during a tense time for the region, just days ahead of Israel's election taking place on Tuesday.

In an interview with Israel's i24 television channel released on Saturday, Netanyahu threatened a "very big surprise" for the Palestinian Authority (PA), which governs parts of the territory.

Hebron Mayor Youssef al-Jaabari said the operation was being "driven by the elections" and that Netanyahu and his ministers were attempting to secure the votes of the far right and the settlers.

On Saturday, thousands gathered in Tel Aviv for a large anti-government demonstration.

The protest was organised by the October Council, a group founded by the families of victims and hostages taken by militants on 7 October 2023, to demand accountability for the failure to prevent the Hamas-led attack.

"Three days before the election, we will hold the culminating event marking three years of struggle to uncover the truth, demand accountability, and establish a state commission of inquiry," the October Council wrote on X ahead of the rally.

The gathering saw the participation of the leaders of the four main opposition parties, including Gadi Eisenkot, the former military chief of staff who is neck and neck with Netanyahu.

items.title: Marina Abramović’s “love letter” to Rome: a gilded bronze donkey
items.summary: Ahead of her 80th birthday, the artist opens up about inspiration, creativity, and her deepest fears. In the Italian capital she unveils a sculpture born out of a dialogue with Alda Fendi
items.content:
The first surprise when you come face to face with Marina Abramović is her long, lingering smiles, one after another. The gaze of the woman who stripped the art audience of its innocence is every bit as stern as the chronicles say, but it is also ironic and amused.

Perhaps it has something to do with the oversized red glasses framing a face impervious to tears—and, as it seems, to time itself. The sense of intimidation the artist inspires via Zoom falls just short of what her world-renowned performances evoke, leaving audiences stunned into absolute silence.

The distance of the screen helps. And above all, this time, we are allowed to ask questions. Starting with one about a little donkey.

We see it stepping forward beside Abramović, who looks straight ahead with the proud, impenetrable expression that has become her trademark. In the background lies the Roman Forum.

No gun, no blade: none of the seventy-two objects that, in 1974 during Rhythm 0 in Naples, the artist placed at the disposal of spectators, authorizing them to do whatever they wished with her body.

This time, she is accompanied by a gentle, patient creature featured in a gilded bronze sculpture—the first Abramović has ever created in this medium.

A “love letter to Rome,” as she defines it herself, as she prepares to turn eighty on November 30. The work, commissioned by the Alda Fendi Foundation-Experiments, will be installed beneath the newly restored Arch of Janus.

We are standing near the Church of Santi Luca e Martina, a Baroque masterpiece by Pietro da Cortona. Outside the windows lies a breathtaking view of the Roman Forum. Inside, the screen displays images of Abramović connecting from New York.

Beside us is Alda Fendi, our host and president of the foundation that bears her name, and an arts patron known for bringing contemporary art and historic heritage together.

The two women speak to each other with the enthusiasm of people who met too late and now want to make up for lost time. The connection glitches more than once. “There’s too much energy circulating between us,” the artist says.

Ms. Abramović, what are you doing in Rome beside a little donkey, looking like a shepherdess or a pilgrim? Does this have anything to do with the months you spent making pecorino cheese in Sardinia back in the 1970s?

“With Ulay—my long-time partner in life and art—I lived in a van for years, traveling with no set destination. In Orgosolo, we stayed for three months. We lived with the shepherds and looked after a flock of a hundred sheep. I learned to milk them and turn milk into cheese. We ate carasau bread; I knitted.

I was fascinated by the traditions of that land, its ancient rituals. Even by the reputation of the bandits: when I asked where they were, the locals replied that they were the bandits. I had very little, but I was free. Those were among the happiest years of my life.”

“No. I was unhappy, very much so. I grew up in a family that belonged to the Yugoslav establishment. My mother was a national heroine; my father was a general. We lived in a kind of red bourgeoisie, all piano lessons and military discipline. It was a controlled existence.

My mother was extremely strict. Up until I was twenty-nine years old, I had to be home by ten at night. I was already an artist, doing performances, exploring the boundaries of freedom, and yet I had to be home by ten.

My grandmother, on the other hand, was deeply religious. She was the one who passed on a sense of spirituality to me. As a child, that dimension allowed me to escape reality. Then I ran away for real. I left home and never went back. I didn't see my mother again until ten years later.”

Did your need to fight for your freedom stem from that childhood?

“That, and the need to prove something. People used to tell me that everything was easy for me, that I was the daughter of important people, that I held a privileged position. I wanted to prove that I could make it on my own. I was very proud of my choice.

Today, I can say that I made it. And above all, I am much happier now than I was in my thirties or forties.”

In 1974, in Naples, for Rhythm 0 , you stood motionless for six hours, allowing the public to do whatever they wanted to your body. Someone cut your clothes, others injured you, and others even pointed a gun at you. Would you ever put an audience in a position to hurt you again?

“Absolutely not. I learned my lesson. In Naples, I realized that if you give people the chance to do anything, they can go so far as to kill you.

Today, my relationship with the audience is completely different. They cannot touch me; they cannot speak to me. I have no need to repeat that experience. I already know what can happen.”

With The Artist Is Present at MoMA in New York in 2010, you spent more than seven hundred hours sitting across from strangers. You are a living archive of humanity. What did you learn?

“That there are no bad people. It is the circumstances, the realities in which we live, that can make us wicked. In people's eyes, I saw suffering, loneliness, melancholy. But also an immense amount of love. I looked 1,565 people in the eye. And I remember those gazes, one by one.

The surprising thing is that, after a while, they were no longer looking at me: they began looking inside themselves. I was merely a mirror. I saw their fragilities, their pains, the emotions we normally hide coming to the surface. Some remained seated for hours, completely losing all sense of time.

And I ended up knowing strangers more intimately than I had ever known members of my own family. It is extraordinary what can happen between two human beings without pronouncing a single word.”

“People wait for hours before they can sit in front of me. And when their turn comes, they are observed by others and by me; they are photographed. They can do nothing; they have nowhere to hide. They must sit there, alone with themselves.

And so they begin to cry. Because suddenly they meet their own feelings and their own loneliness. Some people return. They sleep outside the museum to repeat the experience. It is extraordinary how many things can happen without speaking a single word. The eyes are the soul.”

Alda Fendi: “That is what I love about your art, Marina. You give people the chance to recognize something of themselves. That is the essence of the work we are preparing for Rome. An extraordinary opportunity you are offering to this city.”

Marina Abramović: “It is a confession of the soul. A chance to open oneself up. To me, this work is a love letter to Rome. I want it to contain something people can feel intimately, something that belongs to their lives.”

Alda Fendi explains that the little donkey is no coincidence. As part of the Foundation’s artistic research, the animal has already featured prominently in a series of works exploring spirituality and fragility, inspired by Prayer to Go to Paradise with the Donkeys by French poet Francis Jammes.

A stubborn and gentle creature, burdened for centuries with the weight of humanity, now accompanies a woman famed for turning her own body into a battlefield. Beneath a 4th-century Roman arch, the gilded bronze promises a striking contrast between monumentality and tenderness.

Ms. Abramović, in a world that is dematerializing, do you feel the body is losing its centrality?

“The body is everything. The body is the universe. The body is what we have to know the world and ourselves. But a single lifetime is not enough to fully understand it. You must know the mind, the spirit, your fears, your limits. I have used my body all my life precisely to try to understand how far I could go. And, above all, to free myself from fear.

Naturally, the body ages. And as it ages, it reveals new limitations, reminding you that life is finite. But it continues to teach you something.”

“In nature. I need to be alone, to walk along a river, to hug trees. I need places where you can still feel an ancient wisdom. I have learned a vast amount from Aborigines and shamans. I love monasteries.”

In 1988, you and Ulay set off from opposite ends of the Great Wall of China to meet each other after nearly three months of walking. It was meant to be a celebration of your love, but the interminable delays in obtaining Chinese permits turned it into the most famous farewell in art history. What did you learn from that journey?

“I was always walking in front of everyone. I wanted to be first, as had always happened to me in life. And I didn't understand why the guides kept staying behind me. At one point, I asked why. They answered with a proverb: the most fragile birds fly first . It struck me deeply.

I had always thought that being in front meant being strong, brave, leading others. Instead, according to that ancient wisdom, it could mean the exact opposite. So I changed my position and started walking behind. I learned that it is not necessary to always be first.”

When a love story like the one between you and Ulay becomes a work of art and then the love ends, who gets to keep the artwork?

items.title: Show HN: A Truly Modular Keyboard
items.summary: Article URL: https://github.com/notaroomba/keybytes Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50228115 Points: 109 # Comments: 24
items.content:
Designed in KiCad! There are two boards, the Keybit and the Keyword, and both are 1u (19.05mm x 19.05mm).

A single key with a Cherry MX switch and a CH32V003. Every side has pogo pins for 3.3V, GND and I2C so it can connect to the keyword or to other keybits, and the pads on the corners are for programming.

The main board that the keybits connect to. It is split into two PCBs that stack on top of each other. The top one has the STM32WB55RGV6, the antenna and the flash, and the bottom one has the USB-C, the charger and the buck-boost converter. The 3 pogo pins on the top are for programming the keybits.

Custom designed cases in Onshape , the STEP files are in the cad folder.

items.title: Obama attacks Trump as he campaigns for Democrats ahead of midterm elections
items.summary: Obama said the election was "the last best chance to at least rein in some of the foolishness of this administration".
items.content:
Former US President Barack Obama has attacked the Trump administration over the Iran war and high consumer prices as he hit the campaign trail for Democrats ahead of the US midterm elections.

"This election is our last best chance to at least rein in some of the foolishness of this administration," Obama told crowds in Ohio on Saturday.

Meanwhile, US President Donald Trump touted his administration's immigration and tariff policies at a rally in Georgia, telling supporters "we're in the golden age of America".

The midterm elections on 3 November will decide which party controls Congress for the rest of Trump's term, and therefore how easy it is for the president to carry out his plans.

Early voting has already begun and Trump cast his ballot on Saturday in Florida alongside his wife First Lady Melania Trump.

Obama targeted Trump and his cabinet members while speaking on Saturday in Ohio and Michigan, at one point mocking the president's attempt to redecorate the White House.

"After two years of chaos and cruelty and corruption and incompetence, the likes of which we have not seen in the modern era, you get a chance to say, 'enough is enough'," the former president said in Cleveland.

Obama said he sympathised with voters who rejected Democrats in 2024 over economic and inflation concerns following the Covid pandemic. But he said Trump had only himself to blame for the current state of the economy.

"If you thought everything was too expensive before 'you know who'," he said, referring to Trump without using his name, "everything is more expensive now".

Trump, meanwhile, acknowledged that oil prices were "temporarily high" but said "our country is getting stronger and stronger all the time, and those pump prices are going to come down".

The Republican president has faced significant pressure to lower fuel prices, which have jumped due to the wars in Iran and Ukraine.

Talking up the economy, Trump told the crowd in Perry "we're taking in massive amounts of money through tariffs" and repeated his pledge to offer every adult American a $5,000 (£3,700) payout if Republicans win both chambers of Congress.

He also took aim at the Democrats, telling the crowd they would "loot your wealth" and "annihilate your borders".

Using derogatory language, he accused the Democrats of trying to open up immigration from Libya, Yemen, Haiti and Somalia - countries which he described as "terror-infested".

Describing a previous meeting with several senators, he recalled: "I said, 'Why do we always have to take people from shithouse countries? Why can't we take people from, like, well... Norway, Sweden? Why not Denmark?'"

In Ohio, the current president faced an attack from his predecessor over the war in Iran, with Obama telling Democrat supporters the conflict had given Tehran "veto power" over the Strait of Hormuz.

When asked about the war earlier in the day, Trump said: "I've done it very effectively and I may have to finish it off, or maybe they'll make a deal, but I'm not sure. Either way, we win."

He was also asked whether Melania Trump would would visit Ukraine after the White House announced she secured a ceasefire in a Russian-occupied city. "We will see," he said.

At his afternoon rally, Obama also took a swipe at Trump's efforts to renovate the White House.

"What's with all the gold? He's got the White House looking like Saddam Hussein opened up a Cheesecake Factory," Obama joked.

Obama's rally in Ohio was to show support for ex-Senator Sherrod Brown, who is running to unseat incumbent Republican Senator John Husted, and Amy Acton, who is running for state governor against Republican Vivek Ramaswamy.

Obama criticised Ramaswamy for a campaign ad released last week in which Acton's estranged mother was featured calling her a liar. The ad didn't mention that the woman's husband was charged with raping Acton when she was a child.

"In recent days, we've seen there is no line he will not cross. No low he will not sink to try to get in the limelight," Obama said. "I mean, think about this latest ad he ran."

Acton also spoke at the campaign rally before Obama to argue that Ramaswamy "has chosen to exploit my childhood" to "save his struggling campaign".

items.title: Roborock Saros 20 Neo è il robot aspirapolvere lavapavimenti che toglie di mezzo anche gli imprevisti
items.summary: Tanta automazione, stazione multifunzione e aspirazione da 36.000 Pa. Perché la vera innovazione è dover fare meno per la pulizia ... Leggi tutto
items.content:
I robot aspirapolvere hanno già risolto da tempo il problema più semplice: muoversi per casa raccogliendo polvere e sporco. Ciò che continua a fare la differenza, soprattutto nella fascia più alta del mercato, è tutto ciò che accade quando la casa smette di essere un ambiente ideale.

In pratica, quando ci sono i vari, piccoli ostacoli che sono comuni in un’abitazione normale: come un tappeto più spesso di un altro, una soglia alta o un cavo lasciato a terra. Oppure, semplicemente, la necessità di lavare e asciugare i mop senza che qualcuno debba intervenire ogni volta.

Roborock Saros 20 Neo è un robot che abbina 36.000 Pa di aspirazione a una serie di soluzioni pensate soprattutto per ridurre le situazioni nelle quali l’utente è costretto a preparare la casa prima della pulizia o a intervenire durante il ciclo. In altre parole, è un robot pensato per occuparsi anche degli imprevisti.

Ma c'è un altro motivo: Saros 20 Neo è in sconto a 749 euro su Amazon e sull'eshop di Roborock.

Uno dei limiti più evidenti dei robot aspirapolvere emerge quando incontrano dislivelli, soglie e tappeti. Per superarli, Saros 20 Neo utilizza il sistema AdaptiLift 3.0, progettato per modificare l’assetto del robot in base a ciò che trova davanti a sé. Nell’attività di pulizia permette quindi di superare soglie doppie alte complessivamente fino a 8,8 centimetri , suddivise in due passaggi da 4,5 e 4,3 centimetri. Il sistema è stato progettato per resistere a oltre 20.000 attraversamenti delle soglie, che equivalgono ad anni di pulizia quotidiana.

In più, Saros 20 Neo può sollevare il proprio assetto e gestire tappeti con pelo fino a 3 centimetri . Quando invece il lavaggio rischierebbe di rappresentare un problema oppure si è deciso di aspirare prima i tappeti attraverso l’apposita funzione, i mop vengono rimossi automaticamente quando il robot parte dalla base multifunzione, evitando così di trascinare superfici bagnate sopra i tappeti. Invece attivando la modalità di pulizia profonda dei tappeti, la spazzola principale del Saros 20 Neo rimane in posizione stabile verso il basso durante una seconda passata, per migliorare la raccolta dei detriti rispetto alla normale posizione flottante.

La potenza di aspirazione HyperForce raggiunge i 36.000 Pa , perfetta per aspirare lo sporco anche negli angoli, anche grazie all’inclusione del braccio laterale FlexiArm Arc può estendersi verso l’esterno per raggiungere più facilmente i bordi. A ciò si aggiunge il sistema Dual Anti-Tangle, che lavora insieme alla spazzola DuoDivide per limitare l’accumulo di capelli e peli. Insomma: Saros 20 Neo lascia il pavimento pulito e ordinato e poi non c’è bisogno di perdere tempo a rimuovere i capelli rimasti avvolti nella spazzola.

Per il lavaggio, Saros 20 Neo utilizza due mop rotanti che possono raggiungere una velocità di 200 giri al minuto e applicare fino a 14 N di pressione sul pavimento. Inoltre, Saros 20 Neo riduce fino al 30% l’acqua residua lasciata sul pavimento.

Prima ancora di aspirare o lavare, il robot deve capire che cosa ha davanti. Saros 20 Neo utilizza il sistema Reactive AI Obstacle Recognition, basato su fotocamera RGB e luce strutturata, insieme alla tecnologia VertiBeam.

Grazie a questo sistema avanzato, può riconoscere oggetti comuni che possono trovarsi sul pavimento, come cavi, scarpe, giocattoli, ciotole e altri piccoli ostacoli.

Per anni, uno dei consigli più comuni prima di avviare un robot aspirapolvere è stato togliere da terra tutto ciò che potrebbe confonderlo. Un prodotto come Saros 20 Neo ribalta invece il problema: è il robot che deve imparare a gestire ciò che trova; e il Saros 20 Neo ci riesce molto bene.

Allo scopo di adattare il robot alle esigenze domestiche e non viceversa, Saros 20 Neo misura 7,98 centimetri in altezza. Può sembrare una caratteristica meno evidente e impattante rispetto ai 36.000 Pa di aspirazione, ma le sue dimensioni gli permettono di passare facilmente sotto ai divani e ai letti oltre che sotto i mobili bassi fino a 7,95 cm, che spesso sono fra le zone più complicate per i robot dotati di torrette di navigazione più alte.

Saros 20 Neo ci riesce perché il sistema di scansione dell’ambiente circostante, che normalmente è sollevato per garantire una mappatura precisa, viene automaticamente ritratto e passa a una visuale posteriore a 100°: così il robot continua a sapere come muoversi ma può passare anche in spazi dove altri dispositivi non arrivano.

Ancora più interessante è il modo in cui il robot gestisce la differenza fra una stanza e l’altra. Con SmartPlan 3.0, Saros 20 Neo può adattare il ciclo di pulizia tenendo conto della tipologia di ambiente , dei materiali e dello storico delle sessioni precedenti. Per esempio, può intensificare la pulizia nelle aree che sono state trascurate oppure tornare alla base per lavare nuovamente i mop dopo essere passato in cucina o in bagno.

Inoltre, il Saros 20 Neo sa occuparsi anche di zone della casa che normalmente rischiano di essere trascurate. Contrassegnando manualmente le tende, per esempio, pulisce dietro tende e divisori morbidi, coprendo quindi anche le aree nascosto senza bisogno di sollevarli o regolarli. E quando le porte di una stanza sono chiuse, il Saros 20 Neo prosegue senza urtarle né spingerle, per evitare il rischio di danneggiarle. E se in precedenza ha evitato una zona - magari perché c’era un ostacolo temporaneo o un animale domestico - il sistema è progettato per proseguire l’attività di pulizia altrove e poi ritorna sulla zona non coperta appena è libera. Per di più, SmartPlan 3.0 è un sistema che continua a imparare dalle abitudini di pulizia e quindi migliora nel tempo.

Non è solo il robot a essere dotato di grande autonomia, perché anche la base multifunzione riesce a compiere tante operazioni senza bisogno di intervento. La base multifunzione infatti può svuotare automaticamente il contenitore della polvere, lavare i mop con acqua fino a 100 °C (rimuovendo il 99,99% dei batteri) e asciugarli successivamente con aria calda fino a 55 °C.

Il sistema può anche rilevare il livello di sporco dei mop e decidere di prolungarne il lavaggio oppure richiedere al robot un ulteriore passaggio nell’area appena pulita. Sono previste anche il riempimento automatico con acqua calda e il dosaggio del detergente.

La parte interna della base è rimovibile, così da semplificarne la pulizia quando necessario. È forse qui che si vede meglio il cambiamento avvenuto in questa categoria di prodotti.

Una parte della gestione rimane comunque nelle mani dell’utente. Attraverso l’app Roborock è possibile lavorare sulle mappe, dividere gli ambienti, creare zone escluse, scegliere modalità e intensità della pulizia oppure definire il comportamento sui tappeti.

Anche i comandi vocali possono essere utilizzati direttamente attraverso "Hello Rocky" , anche senza Wi-Fi, che permette di avviare o interrompere la pulizia, indicare una stanza, localizzare il robot oppure modificare aspirazione e quantità d’acqua. Il sistema può funzionare anche offline. Inoltre, supporta il protocollo Matter, che consente di automatizzare le routine e controllare i vari dispositivi della smart home da un’unica piattaforma, che sia Alexa, Siri o Google Home.

items.content:
Why is this worth your time? Essentially, this solves two problems of AI-assisted programming:

(a) the first problem is how to do oversight and what do oversight of and this is solved through the ORRCF (for Options, Recommendation, Rationale, Confidence, Falsifier) question format (in which models are supposed to surface all their doubts with fully fleshed out recommendations, with falsifier, to be approved or overridden)

(b) the second problem is how to scaffold sustainable AI-written code; the ADRs (Architectural Deliberation Records, after Nygard's decision records) written by the models, summarize all the thought process involved in any design decision and provides the blueprint for the code.

In tandem, the records provide both the reason why certain non-obvious design choices were made, from a constant, to a library choice, to an ordering in an operation; and also under what conditions different decisions would be made, for instance, in a different platform, or under different latency requirements, or for a different audience, and so on.

This is a framework I've been working for over a year, that is the starting point of all my projects. It involves a lot of moving parts and my challenge is figuring out onboarding. I'm hoping the plugin, ADRs4AI/plugins, just created and now also submitted to Anthropic's marketplace, will make it easier. I am also in the process of recording introductory videos.

I would like feedback on the onboarding, on what you make of the currently online materials, and how I could make any of this clearer. Thanks!

items.title: The bitter row over military service that could shape Israel's future
items.summary: The ultra-Orthodox community is resisting being drafted into the Israeli army. But will they now bring down the Netanyahu government?
items.content:
Furious protesters are denouncing Israeli security forces as "Nazis" - but this is not a scene from a pro-Palestinian rally on the streets of London or Paris. This clash is in the heart of Israel, in which hundreds of ultra-Orthodox men in white shirts, black fedoras and long black frock coats face off against the military police.

The flashpoint is a building in the city of Modi'in, midway between Jerusalem and Tel Aviv, where a young ultra-Orthodox Jewish (or Haredi) man lives. The police have come to arrest him after he failed to report for military service.

The clash in early October, seen by the BBC in a video, is one of many in recent months in which one of the deepest schisms in Israeli society has become ever more exposed.

This widening fault line is playing out against the backdrop of the wars Israel is currently fighting, including the unresolved conflict against Hamas in Gaza - as well as increasing violence by extremist settlers against Palestinians in the occupied West Bank.

Once a tiny minority, the ultra-Orthodox remain a group apart even as their numbers expand year by year. Currently, they are estimated to make up about 14% of the population, and the birth rate within the community remains far higher than among other Israelis. If their numbers continue to grow at a similar rate, they could make up one-third of the Jewish Israeli population by 2050.

As the ultra-Orthodox community becomes bigger, so has the debate around the expense of supporting them with stipends so they can devote themselves to full-time religious study. Subsidies to the group are estimated to cost the government 35bn shekels (£8.4bn) per year and, until recently, they were exempted from military service.

Now they're no longer an insignificant minority, they're facing pressure to engage more with wider Israeli society.

National security and the economy are two of the key issues this election. That means the division between the ultra-Orthodox and the majority of Israelis who believe they are not contributing their fair share to either is starker than ever.

With no outright majority likely for any current political alliance, and the future of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu in doubt, the role of smaller parties - including Haredi parties - will once again be crucial in deciding who will govern Israel.

To have any chance of staying in power, Netanyahu needs to keep the ultra-Orthodox parties on side, however much pressure there is within Israel for their special status to be diminished.

From the ultra-Orthodox perspective, their social contract with the Israeli state is increasingly coming under pressure. Their all but exclusive focus on the study of Judaism's religious texts - such as the Torah, the Jewish Bible - means their education system is separate and many Haredim are not part of Israel's workforce.

For the ultra-Orthodox, the biggest issue of all is holding on to the exemption from serving in the IDF for students at traditional religious - or yeshiva - institutions. This dates back to the earliest days of the Israeli state when the Haredim were a miniscule community of survivors struggling to rebuild from the near extinction of the Holocaust.

But as Israel has become more embattled after the attacks of October 7, fighting wars on several fronts, their near complete absence from the country's conscription army has become more controversial.

Religious students and their rabbis believe that if young ultra-Orthodox men enter the military, they will be exposed to influences and behaviours that may decisively turn them away from their community. Beyond that, they believe that their staying true to the traditions of their community is vital for the very survival not only of Israel but the Jewish people.

When asked not long after October 7 why the ultra-Orthodox didn't contribute more to the military in such an emergency, one of the community's most senior leaders, Rabbi Dov Landau, said that not only should religious students not serve in the army, but they shouldn't even visit the wounded or attend the funerals of soldiers.

The rabbi said that in a time of such danger, only Torah students could protect Israel spiritually. "Salvation only comes through Torah learning, orderly Torah learning. And any neglect of or disruption to Torah learning, woe and alas for what will happen… The more Torah learners multiply, the more Torah learners increase their learning, the better. They protect us."

It would be a considerable understatement to say that this view is not shared by wider Israeli society. Polls have shown public support for conscripting the ultra-Orthodox surge throughout the war in Gaza. Many see it as a dereliction of responsibility by the Haredi community, made all the more galling by the fact that such a stance comes at the expense of taxpayers. The IDF has bemoaned a deficit in manpower, while many Israelis have had to serve hundreds of days in the past three years.

Dahlia Scheindlin is a leading political consultant and pollster in Israel. She says this issue is critical for Netanyahu and is key to understanding this moment in Israeli society against the backdrop of the war in Gaza, particularly among the political right. "Really the most burning, more immediate issue is the right-wing communities who are furious at the government for protecting the blanket exemption from the IDF at a time when, especially among the right, but really everybody in the Jewish community in Israel, is serving and many dying in these wars."

Two years ago, the Supreme Court ruled that the exemption for ultra-Orthodox men from serving in the military was effectively null and void. That could have meant that those dedicated to full-time religious study would now be drafted.

The reaction from the Haredi community was one of fury. Hundreds of thousands of Haredim held protests, blocking the main highways. And as with the incident in Modi'in, they tried to prevent the arrest of religious students for evading conscription. Protests have continued off and on, and densely-populated Haredi areas are often the backdrops for confrontation with the security forces.

There are two parties that have traditionally represented the Haredi community. One is United Torah Judaism – or UTJ – and represents Ashkenazi Jews, or Jews of European origin. The other is Shas, which was formed later and represents the Sephardi and Mizrahi – Jews from North Africa and the Middle East. They share a core agenda, which puts religious study above all else, including any questions around relations with the Palestinians.

Both UTJ and Shas have been part of Netanyahu's coalition - and they used their political clout to find ways to try to block enforcement of the Supreme Court ruling. On several occasions, they threatened to pull out of the alliance and bring the government down. UTJ acted on this but continued to support the government from outside, while Shas remained within the coalition.

Centre-right politician Gadi Eisenkot, who's shaped up as Netanyahu's main rival in this month's election, does not support their stance. He has made clear his belief that the idea of the ultra-Orthodox constituting a separate state within Israel with its own rules has become increasingly toxic. "A country that sends its best sons and daughters to fight and sacrifice their lives cannot tolerate a reality in which a state within a state exists," he said.

All this has meant that the issue of conscription exemption for ultra-Orthodox men is the number one priority on the electoral agenda of both Shas and UTJ.

A recent remark by a UTJ parliamentary candidate, Eliakim Stark, has raised the temperature further. He compared the plight of ultra-Orthodox men evading the military draft to the persecution of Jews during the Holocaust. It triggered furious rebukes from opposition leaders from across the political spectrum.

Daniel Goldman, an activist who specialises in Haredi issues, says that the two main Haredi parties feel increasingly embattled and less open to compromise.

He says the ultra-Orthodox don't believe that the state really needs their boys to bolster numbers. "It's at least partly down to the fact that the Haredi parties see the state as wanting to take their boys out of the community and change them from ultra-Orthodox to either regular religious or secular, God forbid, as they perceive it," he says. "And so in that environment of tension, they've actually hardened their positions."

Yitzhak Goldknopf from the UTJ, a former minister, has gone so far as to issue an ultimatum: "The Haredim will not change their way of life because there is an army and a war... If there is no choice and they must leave the country, they will leave."

But this is having a clear impact on the electoral fortunes of the Netanyahu coalition - of which Shas in particular has long been a key part. Without them, Netanyahu's alliance would fall short of the more than 60 seats needed for a majority in the Knesset.

Dahlia Scheindlin, the Israeli pollster, says that the refusal to give up the draft exemption by Shas and UTJ is damaging Netanyahu's coalition. "It is one of the main reasons why the coalition is unable to win back the kind of support that they had in 2022 when they won 64 seats," she says. "They're currently polling at about 50 to 52 seats."

items.title: Why the King's Caribbean tour could be 'biggest risk of his reign'
items.summary: The meticulously-planned visit takes in three countries in nine days - but is not without jeopardy.
items.content:
The planning is meticulous and dates back months, sometimes years, but there is always jeopardy.

King Charles III's visit to the Caribbean, which starts on Tuesday, takes him to three countries in nine days: the Bahamas, Guyana and finally Antigua and Barbuda for the Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting (Chogm).

It also throws him directly into the heat of the debate over the payment of reparations - compensation from countries that took part in the slave trade - alongside questions of whether the King should be apologising for the UK's role in what he has previously described as an "appalling atrocity" that leaves an "indelible stain" on history.

"This is the biggest risk of his reign so far with so much just outside of his control," said author and historian Sir Anthony Seldon. "Questions about slavery, reparations and apologies mean the moral integrity of the monarchy is being questioned."

The King will make three significant speeches during the Caribbean trip and will follow government advice not to issue an official apology for Britain's role in the transatlantic slave trade.

A senior royal aide said that the King would "not shy away from the darkest days of our past" but stressed that decisions over apologies and reparations were matters for government.

The current Burnham administration, like those before it, will not pay reparations.

Buckingham Palace says that acknowledging the wrongs of the past will be built into the King's programme in all three countries.

But apologies, reparations, and republicanism are rich pickings for campaigners and protests are likely.

This is the reality for the King and Buckingham Palace, and they are accepting of it.

Those who've worked on the planning of the trip view protests as part of the open debate in the region and security preparations include their possibility.

Lurking in the back of Royal Household minds will also be memories of the last tour by senior royals to the Caribbean in the early part of 2022.

Then, as the Duke and Duchess of Cambridge, William and Catherine found themselves facing criticism over the optics of the trip - images of the royal couple reaching out to touch the outstretched hands of Jamaican children through a wire fence looked clumsy. Engagements designed as tributes to past royal visits appeared outdated. And protests also caused the cancellation of a small part of the schedule.

Everything will have been done to avoid those kinds of missteps on the 2026 Caribbean tour.

The leadership in the Bahamas, Guyana and Antigua and Barbuda will celebrate the King and his work in protecting rainforests, creating cultural ties and reinforcing relationships around trade, energy, and agriculture.

The leaders of all three countries have voiced their support for reparatory justice.

In Antigua and Barbuda and the Bahamas, where the King is head of state, the conversation about becoming a republic has significant support.

Elected officials in the former no longer have to pledge allegiance to the King ending a 40-year tradition of swearing loyalty to the monarch.

"He pulled off an extraordinary triumph with President Trump in his US visit earlier this year and stood up to him and put him in his place in a way that no leader has done - while not incurring his wrath," said Sir Anthony. "If he can deal with the delicate nature of this trip for him personally, for the British monarchy, and the future of the Commonwealth, it could be an enormous success."

This Caribbean tour has to cut through a sea of royal distractions.

The King has spent much of the past three months in Scotland, where he is based over the summer.

It should have been a quieter time in the royal calendar, but it has been quite the opposite.

The surprise return of the Duke and Duchess of Sussex to the UK has been noisy. The level of coverage Harry and Meghan get is unsettling and, at times, irritating for the Royal Family.

The King's youngest son has not yet seen his father in person, but they are said to have talked.

Then enter Earl Spencer, the King's former brother-in-law, with his memoir, Swan Song, criticising the King's response to the death of Diana, Princess of Wales. It triggered a strong pushback from the Palace.

And in recent days, the serious claims made about Meghan's father, Thomas Markle, have drawn his daughter into a complex tale involving global police forces, sexual abuse allegations and further family trauma.

An impactful and successful Caribbean tour is a chance to switch focus.

But if royal stories back home are running hot, it can be hard to focus minds on the King's engagements over four thousand miles (6,437km) away.

Former Foreign Secretary David Lammy, who has strong family ties to the Caribbean, has accompanied the King on a number of trips outside the UK.

"He is our head of state. He is amongst some of the most recognisable figures in the world. For a small country like Guyana, the validation of a state visit is huge," said the Tottenham MP whose father came to the UK from what was then British Guiana and who also has relatives in Antigua and Barbuda. "My mother would forever recall the Queen's visit in 1996."

But there was also a recognition of that royal trip jeopardy.

"Knowing Guyana, Antigua and Barbuda as well as I do, he will be overwhelmingly received positively," Lammy said. "But these are lively democracies in which of course there will be some dissent."

A transatlantic flight, three countries over nine days and about 36 separate engagements when you're closing in on your 78th birthday is an intense schedule. It is also a reminder that the King is still dealing with a cancer diagnosis and having regular treatment. Buckingham Palace has reiterated its position that he is on a "positive trajectory".

Queen Camilla will only accompany the King on the Antigua and Barbuda leg of the visit for Chogm and a number of other engagements, including some around her own areas of interest – literacy and supporting efforts to end violence against women and girls.

The Queen, who will be 80 next July, is known to find the pace and hot conditions of some royal tours gruelling.

This is a trip that comes with potential pitfalls but also the possibility of great reward for the King.

"The King can be an extraordinarily empathetic and in tune figure," Sir Anthony said.

items.title: From Russian cages to Irish sanctuary: The five-year rescue journey of Bu and Tyapa
items.summary: For Bu and Tyapa, the five-year journey from Russia to the Irish countryside was anything but straightforward.
items.content:
After years in cramped cages, two brown bears are adjusting to their new life following a remarkable rescue mission that spanned multiple countries, was disrupted by two major conflicts and involved more than 100 people.

For Bu and Tyapa, the five-year rescue journey from the Republic of Dagestan in Russia to the Irish countryside was anything but straightforward.

One bear had spent their life forced to perform in a circus, while the other was confined to a cage so small they could not stand upright.

Today, the bears are now adjusting to a totally different world among the trees and grass at Wild Ireland, a sanctuary for rescued animals in County Donegal.

Wild Ireland founder Killian McLaughlin first learned about Bu and Tyapa in 2021 and committed to bringing them to safety in Donegal.

The sanctuary, located in Burnfoot, opened in October 2019 and provides a safe space for animals, including brown bears, monkeys, wolves, and lynx.

McLaughlin said the two bears were in extremely poor health when they were first rescued.

Former circus bear Bu had spent years confined to a small indoor cage after being forced to perform.

McLaughlin said Tyapa had lived in a cage measuring just 2.5m by 2.5m by 2m, which was too low for him to stand upright and had no roof, which left him exposed to the harsh winters and blistering summer heat.

The bear had no water dish and relied on a hose for drinking water. McLaughlin said he was being raised to be killed for an eventual taxidermy display.

When the bears were rescued, both were severely malnourished and showed signs of psychological trauma.

Blood tests also revealed serious kidney problems associated with prolonged dehydration.

Russia's invasion of Ukraine in February 2022 made the original transport route through Ukraine impossible, said McLaughlin.

An alternative route through the Middle East was then explored, but plans were disrupted again in February 2026 when the escalating conflict involving Iran led to airspace closures and flight disruptions across the region.

More than 100 people were involved in the rescue operation, including volunteers, lawyers, veterinarians, animal transport specialists, cargo teams and officials in Russia, the United Arab Emirates and Ireland.

In late October 2025, Dima and Yana Kim, who work at Tiger House, a sanctuary near St Petersburg that cares for former circus tigers, embarked on a 36-hour drive to Dagestan to rescue the bears.

Bu and Tyapa had to be cut out of their rusting steel cages, sedated and placed in secure transport crates for the journey back to Tiger House, where they received veterinary treatment and underwent quarantine.

After months of preparation and repeated delays, the bears eventually travelled from Moscow via Abu Dhabi to Dublin, arriving in Ireland in August.

Since arriving at Wild Ireland, McLaughlin said both bears have gained weight, their coats have improved, and follow-up blood tests have shown that their kidney function has returned to normal.

He said their habitat provides woodland, water and room to explore, as well as sheltered areas where they can retreat or move out of public view if they would like some privacy.

"These bears have suffered trauma and the first step of that recovery process is get them back out into the forest, get their paws into the soil and on the grass and get them exploring.

Working with bears is certainly not your everyday job, but for Wild Ireland team member Chloe McElhatton, it's one she absolutely relishes.

Chloe has been working at Wild Ireland for just over a year. She studied zoology at Queen's University Belfast, completing a four-year degree before joining the team.

"This is obviously a very unique job, and it's quite different from what most people would do," she said.

"We've done a lot of work hiding food around the bear habitats, encouraging them to search and forage for it themselves and this promotes their natural behaviours and helps them become more comfortable in that new open space," she said.

"Over time, we've seen their confidence build, and you can see great changes, both physically and mentally, in both of them."

Liam, who is from France, said the bears were one of his favourite animals to see when visiting the park.

"Very big and very impressive," is how he summed up Bu and Tyapa.

"I saw chickens, some wolves and some monkeys and then the bears which were definitely my favourite."

Chris Roberts is from Manorcunningham, about 20 minutes from Wild Ireland, and has been visiting the site ever since it first opened in 2019.

"I've lost count of how many times we've been here, but we really wanted to come down today to see if we could catch a glimpse of Bu and Tyapa.

"We absolutely loved it and are delighted to see them doing so well, especially considering their backstory and the awful conditions they were once kept in."

items.title: In Francia le proteste sono state meno violente
items.summary: C'erano molti più agenti dopo le violenze della scorsa settimana; alla fine della giornata ci sono stati comunque scontri e un migliaio di arresti
items.content:
Come in molte città italiane , anche in Francia sabato sono state organizzate nuove proteste, studentesche e contro il carovita, dopo quelle di sabato scorso. Sono state generalmente più pacifiche: sabato scorso c’erano anche state violenze, incendi e saccheggi di negozi; questa volta ci sono stati alcuni scontri e arresti al termine della giornata.

Le manifestazioni organizzate in varie città della Francia sono state centinaia: si sono tenute a Parigi, Lione, Marsiglia, Nantes, Bordeaux, tra le altre. Secondo il ministero dell’Interno hanno partecipato circa 410mila persone, di cui oltre 100mila solo a Parigi; secondo la Confédération générale du travail, una delle più grandi organizzazioni sindacali francesi, i partecipanti sono stati quasi il doppio, sia in generale che a Parigi.

A Orléans, dove oggi si è tenuto il congresso del partito di estrema destra Rassemblement National guidato da Marine Le Pen, si è aggiunto un altro corteo di protesta, pacifico.

In vista delle manifestazioni di questo sabato il governo francese aveva predisposto un imponente piano di sicurezza con l’obiettivo di evitare che si ripetessero le violenze della settimana scorsa.

C’erano circa 70mila agenti e gendarmi, più o meno 10mila in più rispetto a sabato scorso, nel tentativo di evitare quella che il ministro dell’Interno francese Laurent Nuñez aveva definito in quell’occasione « la perdita del controllo » della situazione; sono state impiegate anche unità speciali delle forze dell’ordine, per esempio quelle normalmente impiegate in attività di antiterrorismo, per sorvegliare alcuni edifici pubblici.

Nelle proteste della settimana scorsa erano stati compiuti atti di vandalismo contro diversi edifici pubblici: soprattutto sedi di municipi, ma anche un ufficio turistico a Lione. Alcuni di questi edifici erano stati incendiati – a Limoges l’incendio aveva portato al crollo di gran parte del tetto del municipio e del campanile che lo sovrastava –, altri danneggiati all’interno. Per evitare danni simili questa volta sono anche stati dispiegati droni, elicotteri, una ventina di veicoli blindati, idranti e unità di polizia a cavallo.

In diverse città erano anche stati vietati alcuni percorsi per protestare, dopo giorni in cui erano stati imposti anche dei coprifuoco; sabato in varie città molti musei e luoghi pubblici come parchi e giardini sono rimasti chiusi o hanno modificato i propri orari d’apertura. A Parigi anche alcuni negozi erano rimasti chiusi e avevano coperto porte e vetrine con pannelli protettivi; almeno 24 fermate della metropolitana sono rimaste chiuse.

Proprio a Parigi un corteo è partito nel pomeriggio da Porte d’Italie e ha raggiunto pacificamente Porte de Vincennes verso le 17; dopodiché, alla fine della manifestazione, sono iniziati gli scontri. Ci sono stati lanci di oggetti agli agenti da parte di alcuni manifestanti, e agenti che li hanno caricati e hanno lanciato lacrimogeni e usato idranti.

In altre città, per esempio a Rennes, gli scontri sono iniziati dopo l’organizzazione di proteste in luoghi in cui era vietato riunirsi, secondo quanto dichiarato dalle forze dell’ordine; ci sono stati scontri anche a Lione, Lille, Marsiglia, Montpellier, Nantes, Bordeaux e Tolosa. Il ministro dell’Interno Nuñez ha detto che nel corso della giornata, in tutto, sono state arrestate un migliaio di persone.

items.title: Fireworks and tear gas as protesters and riot police clash in Paris
items.summary: The BBC's Europe correspondent reports from Paris where mostly peaceful protests turned into unrest after nightfall.
items.content:
Police have clashed with protesters in Paris as some demonstrations in France turned violent on Saturday.

A largely peaceful day of protests turned into unrest after nightfall, as protesters were seen throwing objects and fireworks at police.

Around 70,000 officers were deployed across France for a second consecutive weekend and used tear gas and water cannons to disperse crowds.

The Interior Ministry estimated around 400,000 people took part in Saturday's demonstrations, with nearly 1,000 arrests made.

Europe correspondent Nick Beake reports from Paris, where he says there are few signs the unrest will ease soon.

items.title: Vanessa Trump says she is cancer-free six months after revealing diagnosis
items.summary: The ex-wife of Donald Trump Jr, with whom she shares five children, announced in May that she had been diagnosed with breast cancer.
items.content:
Vanessa Trump, the former wife of Donald Trump Jr, has announced that she is cancer-free following her breast cancer diagnosis earlier this year.

Trump, 48, who has five children with US President Donald Trump's eldest son, said that her recent tests results "came back clear, so I'm finally cancer-free", in a short video on her 19-year-old daughter Kai's Instagram account.

Vanessa and Kai Trump then released a longer video on Saturday, in which they discussed breast cancer awareness, early detection and prevention.

Vanessa Trump separated from Trump Jr in 2018 and announced last year that she had begun dating US pro golfer Tiger Woods.

"October is Breast Cancer Awareness Month, a time to raise awareness about early detection, education, and support for those affected by breast cancer," Kai Trump wrote on Instagram.

"I sat down with my mum and Dr Nicole Saphier to talk about my mum's journey with breast cancer and learn more about prevention and early detection."

Kai's post received over 20,000 likes and hundreds of comments from people offering support and well wishes, including from US singer and media personality Mary Millben.

Vanessa Trump explained in the YouTube video that she experienced arm pain for several months before discovering a pea-sized lump in her breast, which testing confirmed was a cancerous tumour.

"It's a process you have to deal with," she said of the days spent waiting for her test results.

"You have to be mentally strong for yourself because you're going to need the strength to fight whatever challenge it is that's coming towards you."

Trump said she was first diagnosed with breast cancer in April. She publicly announced the diagnosis in May, saying in a social media post that she had undergone surgery and was working on a treatment plan with her medical team.

She eventually had a lumpectomy and radiation treatments, she said.

The average risk of a woman in the US developing breast cancer is about 1 in 8, or 13%, according to the American Cancer Society. The disease also accounts for 30% of all new female cancers every year, it says.

Surgery cures most breast cancers, but if some cancer cells remain, chemotherapy, radiotherapy and endocrine therapy can reduce the long-term risk.

Treatments have been advancing, including more targeted therapies for early breast cancer, new types of hormonal therapies, and more precise and effective radiotherapy.
